    #WEATHER CHECK – ESSENTIAL INFORMATION
    Please be ready on time, late arrivals may miss the balloon.
    ##Weather Conditions
    Safety is always our primary concern. In the unfortunate event that your flight has to be
    cancelled it is for a genuine reason. We do not take risks with the weather. Your flight
    booking is valid for 12 months from purchase (unless otherwise stipulated) and we can
    always try again another day!
    ##Cancellations
    If you cancel within 72 hours of departure or do not show up on the morning you will not
    be given a refund.
    ##WHEN AND WHERE WE MEET
    We meet in the front foyer of the Hyatt Hotel, 120 Commonwealth Ave, Yarralumla.
    The meeting time is at the top of this confirmation. Please be on time, late arrivals may
    miss the balloon.
    ####You will be advised the day prior of the meeting time and confirmation of the flight.
    After your check in, there will be a short briefing and then you will be transported to
    the balloon launch site. The launch site is determined by the pilot on the morning.
    Expect to be with us for approximately 3-4 hours.
    ##BREAKFAST
    If you haven't already ordered it a full buffet breakfast is available after the flight
    at the Hyatt's Promenade Cafe at additional cost for Balloon Aloft passengers and their
    guests. Please contact us at the office prior to your flight if you wish to arrange
    breakfast or contact our ground crew when you check in on the morning of your flight.
    ##WHAT TO WEAR AND BRING
    Wear comfortable clothes as for hiking, i.e. long pants and sturdy shoes that will keep
    your feet warm and dry in the wet grass (not high heels or sandals).
    It will not be any colder in the air than on the ground. Dress in layers, so that you can
    take a jacket or jumper off, so as not to become too warm in the balloon. We suggest you
    bring a cap as it can get warm on your head, underneath the 'burner'. Sunglasses are also
    recommended.
    Bring your camera this is a really fantastic photo opportunity. Personal belongings are
    taken on board at your own risk and should be kept to a minimum.
    #COVID safe information
    - Your temperature may be taken upon arrival. Should your temperature be 38.0 or higher
    you will not be able to undertake your flight but will be able to reschedule for a later
    date.
    - We ask that all passengers adhere to social distancing guidelines while not in the
    balloon or bus.
    - You may be asked to wear a mask on the morning, including while indoors for the flight
    check in, during the bus transfers and /or balloon flight or interactions with other
    passengers or staff.
    - Hand sanitiser will be made available to you to use throughout the morning, but please
    be aware that for safety reasons, hand sanitiser is not able to be carried onboard the
    balloon as it is classed as a flammable liquid.
    **Should you feel unwell in the days before your flight please call 02 6248 8200 and
    speak with one of our Reservations team members about postponing your flight.**
    Be aware **YOU WILL BE CLOSE TO OTHER PASSENGERS** during your outdoor adventure.
    ##Fit to Fly
    Ballooning can involve some active participation and as such, a moderate level of fitness
    and wellbeing is required.
    All members of your party will need to be fit & well with:
    - No significant knee problems,
    - No significant hip problems,
    - No significant back or neck problems,
    - No recent surgeries or broken bones,
    - No other existing conditions that would preclude from following the Pilot's
    instructions; Assuming the landing position with knees bent when instructed to do so,
    Absorbing a small bump when the balloon is landing or would prevent them from holding on
    to the safety handles when the balloon is landing,
    - Are able to stand for one hour un-assisted,
    - Do not weight more than 140kg individually and Children do not weigh more than 50kg
    individually,
    - Are not Pregnant
    ![Description of image](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/4EnAwWPxQEWnpPYwNY7W)
    ##If you have any concerns about your fitness to fly, or any other questions, please call
    02 6248 8200 to discuss.

    In short: We WILL leave without if you are late. 9am. No exceptions.

    If you plan on getting Ubers, expect one or two to cancel on you and expect traffic to be
    really bad. We WILL leave without you if you are late so plan your journey to arrive

    ###Thank you for joining Sydney Kayak on a **Harbour Bridge Breakfast Paddle** adventure.
    Your guide for this adventure is Sam McLeod
    **Schedule:**
    - Meet at the beach in Quibaree Park, Lavender Bay before 7.00am.
    We start at 7.00 so please arrive 10 minutes early so you can complete the paperwork and
    have a toilet stop.
    We need to be on time for this paddle so If you are not there we will leave without you
    and there is no refund.
    We will pack the Kayaks, have a safety and paddle
    technique briefing and the plan is to be on the water by 7.15am.
    - We will paddle under the Harbour Bridge, past the Opera House, Admiralty
    House and Kirribilli House into Neutral Bay where we will have breakfast at
    Thelma and Louise Café.
    - After breakfast we will retrace our route back to Lavender bay.
    **What is supplied:**
    Sydney Kayak supplies the kayaks and kayaking equipment, Breakfast and
    Sunscreen.
    **What to bring:**
    You should bring water and a change of clothes for after the paddle in case you
    get wet. It is rare for anyone to fall in but you can get damp from paddle splash.
    You can bring phones and Cameras but remember there is a risk as they don’t
    float and usually don’t work if dropped in water. For anything with a touch
    screen it is a good idea to have a small cloth to wipe drops from wet fingers off
    the screen as drops on the screen can be sensed as a finger touch and make use
    difficult.
    Anything you don’t want to get wet should be in a zip lock bag as a minimum.
    There is very little room in a Kayak so back packs are best left behind unless
    very small.
    **What to wear:**
    Paddling is a water sport so expect to get splashed.
    Your feet will get wet so water friendly footwear is strongly recommended.
    The clothing Golden Rules - your kayak clothing should:
    - NO COTTON or DENIM - when they get wet, they do not dry and
    remain cold and heavy!
    - When wet, your clothing must stay warm and dry quickly!
    - The key concept to bear in mind is layering. Several thin garments will
    keep you just as warm as a single thicker one, and are much more
    versatile. Remember you’ll need to think about staying cool as much as
    staying warm, and you can always add or subtract layers.
    - A light Nylon Jacket will keep out wind and water. Fleeces are OK.
    Avoid heavy Jackets.
    **What to expect:**
    You will be paddling on the beautiful Sydney Harbour.
    There can be a lot of boat traffic so we can sometimes spend a few minutes
    waiting for Ferries.
    This is an easy paddle of about an hour each way depending on conditions
    **Weather cancellation:**
    In the event of bad weather (rain or high winds), a decision will be made the
    evening 24 hours before the paddle. If you don’t receive a call or txt its going
    ahead.
    **Directions:**
    Quibaree Park is on Lavender Street Lavender bay and can be accessed by car as
    well as being a short walk from North Sydney train station and Milsons point
    Ferry.
    There are two morning Kayak tour groups leaving from Lavender bay.
    We use double kayaks, so look for double kayaks (not the singles) on the little
    beach to the west of the boat ramp. See pictures below.
    ![Description of image](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/LeUqARkHTaK2zWst2NQH)
    **Parking:**
    There is 2 hour free parking in Lavender St which starts at 8.30 am. As we are
    usually back around 10.00 to 10.30 this means you can park without worrying
    about any parking issues. However, if you are late we may not be back by 10.30
    when the rangers start issuing tickets so please arrive before 7.15
    **Important Note:**
    We are on a tight timeframe for this paddle due to Café
    bookings and parking restrictions so we ill leave on time. If you are late we will
    leave without you.
    To ensure you get to enjoy your paddle, and for the convenience of your fellow
    paddlers please arrive early.
    Any questions? Call or text Sam 04 5188 7675.
    Looking forward to paddling with you.

    *Thank you for joining Sydney Kayak on a Seal encounter lunch paddle
    adventure.
    Your guide for this adventure is Sam Mcleod*
    ##Schedule:
    **Lunch Paddle**
    Meet at the Lighthouse end of Station beach on the Pittwater side of Governor
    Philip park, Palm beach at 10.30.
    Please be on time. We will pack the Kayaks, have a safety and paddle technique
    briefing and plan to be on the water by 11.00.
    **Dinner Paddle (Daylight Savings: October - March)**
    Meet at the Lighthouse end of Station beach on the Pittwater side of Governor
    Philip park, Palm beach at 4.30pm.
    Please be on time. We will pack the Kayaks, have a safety and paddle technique
    briefing and plan to be on the water by 5.00.
    **Dinner Paddle (April- September)**
    Meet at the Lighthouse end of Station beach on the Pittwater side of Governor
    Philip park, Palm beach at 3.00pm.
    Please be on time. We will pack the Kayaks, have a safety and paddle technique
    briefing and plan to be on the water by 3.30.
    We will paddle around the back of Barrenjoey Head and spend some time
    looking at the Seals.
    Please note Seals are wild animals in their natural habitat and there are
    regulations regarding how close we can approach.
    Please follow Sam’s instructions at all times.
    When we have had enough of the Seals we will paddle across Pittwater and
    have lunch on a secluded beach. Which beach will depend on the weather
    conditions on the day.
    After lunch/dinner, and a swim if that is your thing, we will head back to Station
    Beach, either directly or, if there is enough time and you have the energy we will
    take the scenic route (other beautiful Pittwater beaches).
    ##What is supplied:
    Sydney Kayak supplies the kayaks and kayaking equipment, Lunch/Dinner and
    Sunscreen.
    ##What to bring:
    You should bring water and a change of clothes for after the paddle in case you
    get wet. It is rare for anyone to fall in but you can get damp from paddle splash.
    You can bring phones and Cameras but remember there is a risk as they don’t
    float and usually don’t work if dropped in water. For anything with a touch
    screen it is a good idea to have a small cloth to wipe drops from wet fingers off
    the screen as they can be sensed as a finger touch and make use difficult.
    Anything you don’t want to get wet should be in a zip lock bag as a minimum.
    There is not a lot of room in a Kayak so back packs are best left behind unless
    very small.
    ##What to wear:
    Paddling is a water sport so expect to get splashed.
    Your feet will get wet.
    Footwear is strongly recommended.
    The clothing Golden Rules - your kayak clothing should:
    - NO COTTON or DENHIM - when it gets wet, it does not dry and
    remains cold and heavy!
    - When wet, your clothing must stay warm AND dry quickly!
    - The key concept to bear in mind is layering. Several thin garments will
    keep you just as warm as a single thicker one, and are much more
    versatile.
    - Remember you’ll need to think about staying cool as much as staying
    warm, and you can always add or subtract layers.
    - A light Nylon Jacket will keep out wind and water. Fleeces are OK. Avoid heavy Jackets
    ##What to expect:
    You will be paddling on beautiful Pittwater.
    Expect stunning Scenery, Seals and often Sea Eagles
    This is an easy paddle of about 2.5 hours of paddling, depending on conditions
    and the paddling ability of the group.
    ##Weather cancellation:
    In the event of bad weather (rain or high winds) A decision will be made the
    evening 36 hours before the paddle so for a Saturday paddle the decision will be
    made Thursday evening. If you don’t receive a call or txt its going ahead.
    ##Directions:
    Governor Phillip Memorial park is at North Palm Beach and can be accessed by
    car as well as being a short walk from bus stop.
    Look for Kayaks on the beach beside the Northern end of the carpark. There are
    Hire Kayaks at the boathouse. Our meeting is further up the beach, closer to
    Barrenjoey Headland.
    ![Description of image](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/B4mplR5tR8ycFdVDSjFK)
    Looking forward to paddling with you.
    Any questions call or text Sam on 04 5188 7675

    Meet on the grass at the Eastern end of the beach in Rose Bay park, below Rose
    Bay Police Station before 10.30am. We start at 10.30 so please arrive early.
    Please be on time. We will pack the Kayaks, have a safety and paddle technique
    briefing and plan to be on the water by 11.00.
    **Dinner Paddle (Daylight Savings: 2nd Oct - 2nd April)**
    Meet on the grass at the Eastern end of the beach in Rose Bay park, below Rose
    Bay Police Station before 4pm. We start at 4pm so please arrive early.
    Please be on time. We will pack the Kayaks, have a safety and paddle technique
    briefing and plan to be on the water by 5pm.
    **Dinner Paddle (3rd April - 1st Oct)**
    Meet on the grass at the Eastern end of the beach in Rose Bay park, below Rose
    Bay Police Station before 3.30pm. We start at 3.30pm so please arrive early.
    Please be on time. We will pack the Kayaks, have a safety and paddle technique
    briefing and plan to be on the water by 4pm.
    Point Piper Kayaks also operate from the Western end of the beach with hourly
    hire. I will meet you at the eastern end of the beach. (Right hand end of beach when
    facing the water)
    There is usually plenty of parking in local streets.
    Please note there are no longer any toilets or change facilities near Rose bay
    park.
    We will paddle across Rose bay to Milk beach. A short stop at Milk beach for
    photos, a stretch, any fine tuning of kayak adjustments and a swim if you are
    keen. You can also walk up to Strickland House, one of Sydney’s classic historic
    grand homes.
    From Milk beach we paddle to Shark Island where we have lunch/dinner.
    After lunch/dinner and another swim (if you are inclined) we paddle back to
    Rose bay.
    ##What is supplied:
    Sydney Kayak supplies the kayaks and kayaking equipment, Lunch or Dinner, and
    Sunscreen.
    ##What to bring:
    You should bring water and a change of clothes for after the paddle in case you
    get wet. It is rare for anyone to fall in but you can get damp from paddle splash.
    You can bring phones and Cameras but remember there is a risk as they don’t
    float and usually don’t work if dropped in water. For anything with a touch
    screen it is a good idea to have a small cloth to wipe drops from wet fingers off
    the screen as they can be sensed as a finger touch and make use difficult.
    Anything you don’t want to get wet should be in a zip lock bag as a minimum.
    There is very little room in a Kayak so back packs are best left behind unless
    very small.
    ##What to wear:
    Paddling is a water sport so expect to get splashed.
    Your feet will get wet.
    Footwear is strongly recommended and expect it to get wet.
    The clothing Golden Rules - your kayak clothing should:
    - NO COTTON or DENIM - when it gets wet, it does not dry and
    remains cold and heavy!
    - When wet, your clothing must stay warm AND dry quickly!
    - The key concept to bear in mind is layering. Several thin garments will
    keep you just as warm as a single thicker one, and are much more
    versatile.
    - Remember you’ll need to think about staying cool as much as staying
    warm, and you can always add or subtract layers.
    - A light Nylon Jacket will keep out wind and water. Fleeces are OK. Avoid heavy Jackets
    ##What to expect:
    You will be paddling on the beautiful Sydney Harbour.
    There can be a lot of boat traffic and Seaplanes so we can sometimes spend a
    few minutes waiting for Ferries.
    This is an easy paddle of about an hour and a half each way depending on
    conditions and the paddling ability of the group.
    ##Weather cancellation:
    In the event of bad weather (rain or high winds) A decision will be made the
    evening 36 hours before the paddle so for a Saturday paddle the decision will be
    made Thursday evening. If you don’t receive a call or txt its going ahead.
    ##Directions:
    RoseBay park is on New South Head Rd Rosebay and can be accessed by car as
    well as being a short walk from the bus stop and Rose bay Ferry.
    ![Description of image](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/lA2jZuEtQ0S3JmLisECZ)
    Looking forward to paddling with you.
    Any questions or issues call Sam on 04 5188 7675.

    #🏝️ Cook Island Trip – Confirmation & Safety Info
    We’re excited to have you joining us for a trip at Cook Island (Jungarra Ngarrian) — one
    of Australia’s top marine reserves!
    ###Please read the key info below to ensure a smooth and safe day.
    ---
    **1. Sign Your Waiver**
    All participant must complete the digital waiver before arrival.
    You'll find the link in your booking confirmation email.
    Please complete it in advance to avoid delays at check-in.
    ---
    **2. Meeting Point & Timing**
    Gold Coast Dive Centre
    2/54–56 Paradise Ave, Miami QLD
    Please arrive at the time shown on your booking
    (e.g., for a 6:30 trip, check in by 6:30).
    We can’t accommodate early arrivals, but there will be plenty of time to get ready once
    checked in.
    ---
    **3. Parking**
    Free on-street parking nearby.
    Please allow extra time for parking, especially during busy periods or roadworks
    ---
    **4. Proof of Certification**
    Certified divers must bring proof of certification (physical or digital), showing:
    - Your full name
    - Photo
    - Your certification level
    - The certifying agency
    Logbooks are not accepted.
    If you’re SSI certified and can’t find your card, contact us at least 24 hours in
    advance, and we’ll try to look it up.
    ---
    **5. Diving Ability, Confidence & Fitness**
    Cook Island is an open-ocean site. Conditions can vary and may include currents, swells,
    and winds.
    Divers should be confident, fit and competent to dive in open-water conditions.
    If unsure about your skills, we strongly recommend booking a private guide.
    While group dives are guided, divers are expected to be self-sufficient, capable of
    managing their equipment and confident in their skills to avoid affecting the group.
    The minimum certification level for regular dives is SSI Open Water Diver or equivalent;
    below this (e.g., SSI Scuba Diver) requires a private guide.
    ---
    **6. Recent Diving Experience**
    If you haven’t dived in 12+ months or more, you must complete the SSI Scuba Skills
    Update.
    Divers with 250+ logged dives may be eligible to complete a Pool Check-Out Dive instead.
    If it has been 4 years or more since your last dive, you will need to repeat the Open
    Water Diver course.
    ---
    **7. Weather & Plan Changes**
    Cook Island is weather-dependent, and sometimes trips get cancelled due to conditions.
    Weather is unpredictable and cancellations are beyond our control.
    We appreciate your patience and understanding as we prioritise safety.
    ---
    **8. Seasickness & Remedies**
    Due to the location of Cook Island, seasickness can be an issue.
    We recommend taking a seasickness remedy (e.g., Travacalm, Travalcalm HO, or Kwells) 30
    minutes before boarding.
    Bring extra remedies with you — Natural remedies (like ginger) are not as effective.
    ---
    **9. What to Bring**
    Pack light — space on the boat is limited!
    Only bring the essentials:
    - swimmer
    - towel,
    - sunscreen
    - water
    - light snack
    Avoid large bags or bulky items.
    ---
    **10. Gear Handling**
    You’ll carry your own gear from the trailer to the boat (approx. 50m).
    Please handle all equipment with care.
    After the trip:
    - Return all gear to the trailer at the jetty
    - Once back at the dive centre, rinse the gear you used in the designated wash area
    - Turn wetsuits right-side out before placing them in the rinse station
    Thanks for helping us look after shared gear.
    ---
    **11. Boating Etiquette**
    - Always wear your life jacket when instructed
    - Stay seated when the boat is in motion
    - Maintain three points of contact when walking on the boat
    - Stay clear of running engines
    - Pay attention to the safety briefings
    - Respect everyone’s space
    - Keep personal items tidy and out of the way
    - Never throw anything overboard
    ---
    **12. Diving Etiquette**
    - Arrive on time and be ready
    - Be a good buddy, look out for each other
    - Be self-sufficient with your gear
    - Respect marine life and fellow divers.
    - Practice excellent buoyancy control
    - Follow the SSI Blue Oceans Philosophy: don’t touch, don’t take
    ---
    **13. Best Practices & Dive Briefing**
    - Giant stride entry off the Ocean Adventurer
    - Max depth: OW 18m, AOW 30m
    - No-decompression dives only
    - Max bottom time: 45 minutes
    - Surface interval: 30 minutes
    - Always dive in Buddy Teams and complete a pre-dive check
    - Lost Buddy Procedure: 1-minute search → ascend → inflate SMB → signal the boat
    Air Guidelines:
    - 100 bar = turn around
    - 70 bar = begin ascent
    - 50 bar = minimum surfacing pressure
    Safety stop 3/5 minutes at 5 metres on all dives
    ---
    **Surface Interval**
    - After the first dive, change tanks immediately once safely back on the boat
    - Reassemble and secure your equipment without delay so you are fully prepared for the
    second dive
    - Once your gear is organised and ready, relax and enjoy your surface interval
    Keep weight belts, masks, and fins neatly stored and clear of walkways and seating areas
    at all times.
    ---
    **Surface Hand Signals (When on the Surface)**
    If communicating with the boat:
    - OK → Form a clear “OK” sign above your head\
    - Not OK → Raise one arm straight up above your head
    - Help / Distress → Wave one arm side to side above your head until assisted
    Always stay with your buddy and deploy your SMB if required.
    ---
    **Emergency Recall**
    If you hear:
    - Continuous loud banging on the hull
    - Repeated engine revving
    This indicates a full recall to the boat.
    Stop immediately, stay with your buddy, and return directly to the vessel.
    ---
    **Exit procedure**
    - Approach the boat and wait for crew instruction
    - Keep your mask and regulator in place until instructed otherwise
    - Hand up loose equipment if instructed
    - Remove weights and fins before boarding while holding the ladder
    - Board carefully using three points of contact
    Once onboard:
    - Remove your regulator once stable on deck
    - Secure your mask either on your face or around your neck — do not carry it loosely
    - Store fins and weight belts neatly in the designated area
    - Keep all gear clear of walkways and seating areas
    - Avoid placing equipment on benches unless instructed
    ---
    **14. Personal Items**
    Gold Coast Dive Centre isn’t responsible for personal items.
    Any gear or items brought on the trip are at your own risk. We are not liable for loss,
    theft, or damage.
    Please check your belongings before leaving. Unclaimed items will be disposed of after a
    week.
    We do not provide storage.
    ---
    #🐢Cook Island Marine Reserve Code of Conduct
    ###Cook Island is a protected aquatic reserve. Help us protect it.
    ---
    - Look, don’t touch marine life, even shells
    - Keep your distance — Don’t chase or crowd animals
    - Stay 3+ metres from turtles and never block their path
    - No feeding or baiting marine life
    - Don’t rest or grab rocks or reef
    - Control your fins to avoid contact with reef or sediment
    - Maintain buoyancy and stay horizontal above the seabed
    - Secure all gear to prevent dragging
    - Avoid flash or prolonged light when photographing
    - Use reef-safe sunscreen or wear protection
    - Leave artefacts undisturbed
    - Remove floating litter if safe to do so
    ---
    **By completing your booking, you acknowledge that you’ve read and understood the safety
    guidelines and requirements outlined above.**
    Thank you for diving responsibly and helping us protect this special marine environment.
    **Gold Coast Dive Centre Team**
    ---

    **ITINERARY**
    **09:30am– Arrive at Cambridge Town Hall. Shuttle transfer to Hooker Rd / Velodrome.**
    **09.35am –Guided ride from Hooker Rd / Velodrome to Mighty River Domain** Bike induction
    for RAW mountain bike or e-bike hires.
    Starting from the Velodrome, this scenic section of the Te Awa River Ride follows the
    Waikato River through the Cambridge Art Precinct, past public sculptures and riverfront
    pathways, before making its way through the charming Cambridge township. From there, the
    trail continues alongside the river with a mix of boardwalks, bridges, and lakeside views
    as you ride out towards Mighty River Domain at Lake Karapiro.
    This ride offers a relaxed mix of nature, local culture, and stunning river scenery,
    making it best suited to beginner to intermediate riders, families, couples, and anyone
    looking for an enjoyable half-day cycling experience at a comfortable pace.
    Check out the official Te Awa River Ride website:
    https://www.te-awa.org.nz/
    **12:00pm - Complete your ride at Mighty River Domain**
    If there is enough time, you can grab a quick bite to eat or coffee from the local cafe,
    Podium Cafe.
    **12.15pm - Return Shuttle from Mighty River Domain to Cambridge Town Hall**
    ** The above timings are approximate.
    **HIGHLIGHTS**
    * Scenic riverside riding along the Waikato River.
    * The Cambridge Art Precinct with unique sculptures and public art.
    * Riding through the charming Cambridge township cafés and river paths.
    * Boardwalk and lakeside trail sections.
    * Finishing at beautiful Lake Karapiro and Mighty River Domain.
    **CHECK-IN DETAILS**
    Meet at Cambridge Town Hall, there is plenty of public car parking within the vicinity.
    [View TARR Info sheets April
    2026.pdf](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/noH2m8iJSDVOVZw7EjKV)
    Allow plenty of time and check Google Maps for travel;
    * 2 hours and 15 mins from Auckland
    * 1 hour and 20 mins from Tauranga
    * 1 hour and 15 mins from Rotorua

    #🌙 Dusk & Night Dive – Confirmation & Safety Info
    We’re excited to have you joining us for a trip at Cook Island (Jungarra Ngarrian) — one
    of Australia’s top marine reserves! Please read the important info below carefully to
    help make your trip smooth, safe, and unforgettable.
    **1. Sign Your Waiver**
    To participate, you must complete your digital waiver before your dive day.
    You’ll find the link in your booking confirmation email.
    📌 Please ensure this is done in advance to avoid check-in delays.
    **2. Meeting Point & Timing**
    Arrive at: Gold Coast Dive Centre
    📍 2/54–56 Paradise Ave, Miami QLD
    🕒 Please arrive at the time shown on your booking (e.g., for a 3:00 trip, check in by
    3:00).
    We can’t accommodate early arrivals, but there will be plenty of time to get ready once
    checked in.
    **3. Parking**
    🅿️Free on-street parking nearby. Please allow extra time for parking, especially during
    busy periods or roadworks
    **4. Proof of Certification**
    Certified divers must bring proof of certification (physical or digital), showing: Your
    full name, photo, your certification level (e.g. Open Water), the certifying agency (e.g.
    SSI, PADI) 🛑 Logbooks are not accepted.
    📌 If you’re SSI certified and can’t find your card, contact us at least 24 hours in
    advance, and we’ll try to look it up. We can only verify SSI certifications.
    🚫 No proof = no diving = no refund.
    **5. Diving Ability, Confidence & Fitness**
    Cook Island is an open-ocean site, and conditions can vary. Strong currents, swells, and
    winds are common. Divers must be confident, fit, and competent enough to dive in these
    conditions. Winter temperatures can drop to 19°C, but usually average around 22°C.
    📌 If unsure about your skills, we strongly recommend booking a private guide. While group
    dives are guided, divers are expected to be self-sufficient, capable of managing their
    equipment and confident in their skills to avoid affecting the group. The minimum
    certification level for this dive is SSI Open Water Diver or equivalent, with at least 20
    logged dives, and having recent dive experience within the past 6 months. 📌 All divers
    are required to carry: two torches (a primary and a backup), a dive knife and a surface
    marker buoy (SMB or DSMB).
    **6. Weather & Plan Changes**
    Cook Island is weather-dependent, and sometimes trips get cancelled due to conditions.
    While this can be frustrating, safety is our top priority. Please understand that weather
    conditions are unpredictable, and cancellations are beyond our control. We appreciate
    your patience and kindness—our team is working to ensure a safe experience for everyone.
    **7. Seasickness & Remedies**
    Due to the location of Cook Island, seasickness can be an issue. We recommend taking a
    seasickness remedy (e.g., Travacalm, Travalcalm HO, or Kwells) 30 minutes before
    boarding. Bring extra remedies with you, 📌 as natural remedies (like ginger) are not as
    effective.
    **8. Gear Handling**
    You’ll carry your own gear from the trailer to the boat (approx. 50m).
    After the trip, return and rinse the gear you used — your help is appreciated!
    🧰 Essential gear is provided at no extra cost if needed.
    💬 Stay after the dive to help wash gear and share your dive stories!
    **9. Boating Etiquette**
    - Always wear your **life jacket** when instructed
    - **Stay seated** when the boat is in motion
    - Maintain **three points of contact** when walking on the boat
    - Stay clear of **running engines**
    - **Pay attention to the safety briefings**
    - **Respect everyone’s space**
    - Keep personal items tidy and out of the way
    - **Never throw anything overboard**
    **10. Diving Etiquette**
    - **Arrive on time** and be ready
    - **Be a good buddy**—look out for each other
    - **Be self-sufficient** with your gear
    - **Respect marine** life and fellow divers.
    - Practice excellent **buoyancy control**
    - Follow the **SSI Blue Oceans Philosophy**—Don’t touch, don’t take
    **11. Boating and Safety After Diving**
    After your final dive, please **remain seated with your life jacket on** while the boat
    returns to shore. To help the crew maintain visibility and safety at night, keep your
    light in hand and switched on until we've arrived to the jetty.
    **12. Best Practices & Dive Briefing**
    - **Giant stride entry** off the Ocean Adventurer
    - Max depth: **OW 18m, AOW 30m**
    - **No-decompression dives only.**
    - Max bottom time: **45 minutes.**
    - Surface interval: **30 minutes**
    - Always dive in **Buddy Teams** – complete a **pre-dive check**
    - **Lost Buddy Procedure:** 1-minute search → ascend → inflate SMB → signal the boat
    - **Air Guidelines:** 100 bar = turn around, 60 bar = begin ascent, 50 bar = minimum
    surfacing pressure
    - **Safety stop** 3/5 minutes at 5 metres on all dives
    - **Emergency recall:** listen for **continuous banging** or a **revving engine**
    - **Exit procedure:** remove fins and weights before boarding. Keep mask & regulator on
    until safely onboard
    **13. Using Lights**
    - Check both **primary and backup lights** before entering the water
    - **Turn on your light before entering the water and do not switch it off underwater**
    - **Turn off your light only once you're back on the boat and your gear is secured**
    - **Avoid shining lights directly at your buddy’s eyes**
    - **Use lights responsibly – avoid prolonged lighting on marine life**
    - **Hold torch at arm’s length** to reduce backscatter
    - **Aim at your buddy’s torso** to signal or attract attention
    - **Review hand signals using light** before the dive
    - Minimise use of light in **turbid water** to avoid glare or reduced visibility
    - Keep your light on and in hand **during the return**
    **14. What to Bring**
    Pack light—space on the boat is limited! Only bring the essentials: towel, hat &
    sunglasses, water, light snack. Avoid large bags or bulky items.
    **15. Personal Items**
    Gold Coast Dive Centre isn’t responsible for personal items. If you bring gear or
    belongings, it’s at your own risk. We won’t be liable for lost, stolen, or damaged items.
    Please check your belongings before leaving. Unclaimed items will be disposed of after
    three weeks. We do not provide storage.
    #🐢Cook Island Marine Reserve Code of Conduct
    Cook Island is a **protected aquatic reserve.** Help us protect it:
    - **Look, don’t touch:** Avoid all marine life, even shells
    - **Keep your distance:** Don’t chase, corner, or crowd animals
    - **Respect turtles:** Stay 3+ metres away, don’t block surfacing
    - **No feeding:** No baiting or interaction
    - **Don’t rest or grab rocks or reef**
    - **Control your fins:** Avoid kicking the reef or sediment
    - **Maintain buoyancy:** Stay horizontal, 1m above the seabed
    - **Secure your gear:** Nothing dangling or dragging
    - **No flash** or prolonged light use when photographing
    - **Use reef-safe sunscreen** or cover up instead
    - **Leave artefacts** undisturbed
    - **Remove floating litter** (if safe) — avoid disturbing debris with marine growth
    #✅ Confirmation of Understanding
    **By completing your booking, you acknowledge that you’ve read and understood the safety
    guidelines and requirements outlined above.**
    Thank you for diving responsibly and helping us protect this special marine environment.
    📞 Questions? Just give us a call at 07 55 720 511.
    We can’t wait to welcome you to the water!
    **The Gold Coast Dive Centre Team**
    I need to add:

    surface marker buoy are mandatory for all night divers.
    **10. Boating and Safety After Diving** While sailing back, remain seated with your life
    jacket on until reaching the jetty. Keep a light on in your hand to ensure visibility and
    safety on the return trip.

    **Please read the SAFETY INFORMATION below. 👇 It is important for your safety and
    enjoyment.**
    ##Sign your Waiver
    You as a participant must sign the waiver to be able to take part in this activity. So
    please click on the link above ☝️ and **Sign Digital Waiver** to complete your
    registration before your diving day.
    ##Meeting Point and Timing
    Please arrive at Gold Coast Dive Centre, 2/54-56 Paradise Ave Miami.
    Check-in times are the times shown on the booking (eg: for a 6:30 dive you need to be at
    the shop to check-in at 6:30). Please don't show up earlier for trips as we are unable to
    accommodate guests until the designated check-in times; there is adequate time after
    check-in to get everyone sorted.
    ##Parking
    We have Customer Parking Only, 2 hrs max at Gold Coast Dive Centre but there is free
    on-street parking on Paradise Ave.
    ##Proof of Certification
    If you are booked in for a certified dive you are legally required to provide visual
    proof of dive certification, which needs to be seen by the member of staff that checks
    you in. Certification can be a physical dive card or digital copy but it must have a
    photo, name, certification level and certifying body (log books are not proof of
    certification). If you cannot find your dive certification, we can look it up for you,
    but please request this at least 24 hours before diving via email. If no proof of
    certification can be shown or found on the day of diving, we will be unable to take you
    diving, and no refunds or changes will be given.
    ##Diving Ability, Confidence and Competence
    Cook Island Marine Reserve is an open ocean dive site that is frequented by all levels of
    divers; We are unable to predict a divers' competence by their qualifications or
    experience; this varies with every individual. However, please be aware that there can be
    strong swells, strong currents, strong surges, cold water and strong winds and it is a
    requirement that divers have the ability, fitness, confidence and competence to dive in
    such conditions. In the winter months, the temperature can drop as low as 19 degrees but
    averages around 22 degrees. If you are unsure about your ability to dive in the
    conditions above, you should book a private guide to look after you. Regular dives with
    Gold Coast Dive Centre are guided group dives, and as such, divers need to have the
    competence, ability and confidence at a level that won't negatively impact the group. We
    do try to group divers according to their experience but this is not always possible. If
    you or anyone in your booking are not a confident diver or there is any history of
    previous problems diving, please also book a private guide to give the attention needed.
    The minimum certification level is Open Water Diver, if you are below this certification
    level (eg: SSI Scuba Diver) you will need to book a private guide. A Scuba Skills Update
    Refresher Course will be required if anyone in the booking hasn't dived within 12 months.
    If no diving in four years or more, then an SSI Open Water Course will have to be redone.
    ##Short-notice plan updates may be sent
    Cook Island is one of the most weather-dependent sites on Australia's east coast, we
    patiently wait for the right conditions and then dive. If trips are cancelled due to
    weather, please understand this is for safety reasons (yours and ours) and is outside of
    our control. We know cancellations can be frustrating but please understand that the
    weather and sea conditions can be unpredictable and changeable and, are outside of our
    control. Please be kind and polite to our staff who are only working towards a safe
    operation. We have a zero-tolerance policy for rudeness or aggression towards our
    customers and team.
    ##Weather, Swell and Seasickness Remedies
    Cook Island's position is just south of the often treacherous Tweed River Bar. We
    strongly recommend taking a seasickness remedy 30 minutes before boarding (as well as the
    night before if you want extra insurance) and bringing the rest with you. Travacalm
    original, Travalcalm HO and Kwells are 3 recommended types. Ginger/Natural remedy does
    not work.
    ##Cook Island Marine Reserve Code of Conduct
    Cook Island Marine Reserve is part of the NSW National Park. It is an Aquatic Reserve
    known as Turtle Sanctuary and it is home to a permanent population of Sea Turtles, and
    several threatened or protected species. Please follow the Code of Conduct when visiting
    the Cook Island Waters: no touching, collecting, damaging, feeding or moving marine life.
    Look and keep memories, but don’t touch and don’t chase or harass, please be mindful with
    your camera.
    ##Dive Etiquette
    - Please give yourself plenty of time to arrive and prepare.
    - Good Buddy Behavior and Be self-sufficient.
    - Stow your equipment properly.
    - Respect Marine Life and Other Divers.
    - Be mindful of your position in the water.
    - Take only photos, leave only bubbles.
    - Use the right rinse bucket.
    ##Best Practices and Dive Briefing
    **Please read this safety information. It is important for your safety and enjoyment.**
    - Giant Stride Entry on Ocean Adventurer.
    - Maximum Depth of Dive applies to Certification level (OW 18m, AOW 30m).
    - Make all dives no-decompression dives.
    - Maximum Bottom Time: 50 minutes.
    - Divers to dive in Buddy Team. Complete pre-dive safety Buddy Check before entry.
    - Lost Buddy Procedure (if alone, 1 min search, then return slowly to the surface,
    inflate safety sausage and signal to the Boat Crew "I Lost my Buddy!" Lost Buddy Team
    from the group, complete your dive together).
    - Low/Out of Air Procedures (Confirm Signals with Buddy).
    - 100 bar turnaround point, 60 bar to start ascending. (Indicate both to dive leader).
    - The minimum returning tank pressure is 50 bar.
    - Safety Stop to be completed at the end of each dive (3 minutes at 5 metres depth).
    - Emergency recall to boat procedure (Continuous banging sound from boat or leader,
    continuous roaring Boat Engine).
    - Exit: remove fins and weight belt before boarding, please leave your mask on and your
    regulator in. Hold on to the boat while taking your fins off.
    - Protect the Marine Park: Practice good buoyancy, No touch, No take.
    ##What to Bring
    Diving certification, hat, sunscreen, snacks, water, camera, sunglasses, swimmers, towel,
    and anything you need for a day out in the sun and water. Otherwise, we are a Dive Centre
    and Retail Shop offering a wide variety of dive Gear to suit your needs and budget, there
    is a food machine in the shop.
    ##Personal Items
    Gold Coast Dive Centre and its employees take no responsibility for personal items or
    dive gear that are brought onto our property or used during activities whether lost,
    stolen or damaged. With any activity, there is a risk of damage to personal gear from
    handling or normal use. Personal items are brought onto the property and stored or used
    at the owners' own risk. After your activity, please double-check that you have
    everything with you before leaving. If personal items are not collected, they will be
    disposed of after three weeks.

    Risk Disclosure
    Mountain biking is an adventurous sport with inherent risks. Participants may encounter
    steep and uneven slopes; unavoidable obstacles such as rocks, roots, and drops; narrow or
    off‑camber trails with reduced traction; sudden changes in trail conditions; and the
    potential for falls or collisions. Treadmark prioritises safety through expert
    instruction, proactive group management, and well‑planned sessions; however, unexpected
    incidents can occur and injuries are possible.
    Participant Acknowledgement
    By confirming your booking and participating, you acknowledge that you understand the
    nature of mountain biking and its risks; that failure to follow safety instructions or
    incorrect use of equipment may increase your risk of injury; and that while Treadmark
    takes all reasonable precautions, you remain ultimately responsible for your own safety
    and riding decisions.
    Refunds & Credits
    Once the program begins, bookings are non‑refundable. If you cancel seven or more days
    before your first session, you may choose either a full refund less a \$25 administration
    fee or a credit for future use valid for six months. Passes are non‑transferable.
    Weather & Operational Cancellations
    Sessions run in most conditions, including rain. If weather or trail conditions are
    deemed unsafe—such as high winds, lightning, or official trail closures—the session will
    be rescheduled or credited. Where Treadmark cancels, you will receive either a
    replacement session or a session credit. For events that include lift passes or rentals,
    full refunds for those specific items will be provided if cancellation is due to weather.
    Health & Safety Requirements
    A helmet in good condition is mandatory for all participants. Gloves, knee pads, and a
    well‑maintained mountain bike suitable for the terrain are strongly recommended. Please
    inform instructors of any injuries, medical conditions, or recent surgeries that may
    affect your riding. You are expected to ride within your skill level and to follow all
    safety instructions provided by coaches and mountain staff.
    What to Bring
    Unless already rented through Treadmark, please bring a full‑face helmet and knee pads, a
    chest protector, sturdy shoes suitable for mountain biking for all lift access areas.
    Half face helmets for pedal access are ok.
    lunch or money for lunch along with snacks and water. Adequate food, hydration, and
    clothing suitable for changing conditions will help ensure a safe and enjoyable session.
    Media Policy
    Treadmark may capture photographs or short videos during sessions for promotional
    purposes. By confirming your booking, you authorise the use of your images in a
    non‑identifiable manner for marketing. Images will not show full faces or identifiable
    features unless you have provided explicit consent. We prioritise privacy and, where
    consent has not been provided, images used will be generic and non‑identifying. You may
    opt out of all future use of your images at any time by emailing
    [management@treadmark.co.nz]; opt‑outs apply from the time of request forward and do not
    require deletion of materials already published.
    Code of Conduct
    All participants are expected to respect the trails, fellow riders, and the coaching
    team. We maintain a positive, supportive environment with no ego and no pressure. Please
    follow all safety instructions and ride with established trail etiquette in mind to
    promote a safe and welcoming space for everyone.
    Contact
    For questions, changes, or opt‑out requests, please contact management@treadmark.co.nz
    Agreement
    By confirming your booking, you confirm that you have read, understood, and agree to this
    Program Policy, including the Risk Disclosure and Media Policy sections above.

    **Please read the SAFETY INFORMATION below. 👇 It is important for your safety and
    enjoyment.**
    ##Sign your Waiver
    You as a participant must sign the waiver to be able to take part in this activity. So
    please click on the link above ☝️ and **Sign Digital Waiver** to complete your
    registration before your diving day.
    ##Meeting Point and Timing
    Please arrive at Gold Coast Dive Centre, 2/54-56 Paradise Ave Miami.
    Check-in times are the times shown on the booking (eg: for a 6:30 dive you need to be at
    the shop to check-in at 6:30). Please don't show up earlier for trips as we are unable to
    accommodate guests until the designated check-in times; there is adequate time after
    check-in to get everyone sorted.
    ##Parking
    We have Customer Parking Only, 2 hrs max at Gold Coast Dive Centre but there is free
    on-street parking on Paradise Ave.
    ##Proof of Certification
    If you are booked in for a certified dive you are legally required to provide visual
    proof of dive certification, which needs to be seen by the member of staff that checks
    you in. Certification can be a physical dive card or digital copy but it must have a
    photo, name, certification level and certifying body (log books are not proof of
    certification). If you cannot find your dive certification, we can look it up for you,
    but please request this at least 24 hours before diving via email. If no proof of
    certification can be shown or found on the day of diving, we will be unable to take you
    diving, and no refunds or changes will be given.
    ##Diving Ability, Confidence and Competence
    Cook Island Marine Reserve is an open ocean dive site that is frequented by all levels of
    divers; We are unable to predict a divers' competence by their qualifications or
    experience; this varies with every individual. However, please be aware that there can be
    strong swells, strong currents, strong surges, cold water and strong winds and it is a
    requirement that divers have the ability, fitness, confidence and competence to dive in
    such conditions. In the winter months, the temperature can drop as low as 19 degrees but
    averages around 22 degrees. If you are unsure about your ability to dive in the
    conditions above, you should book a private guide to look after you. Regular dives with
    Gold Coast Dive Centre are guided group dives, and as such, divers need to have the

    do try to group divers according to their experience but this is not always possible. If

    level (eg: SSI Scuba Diver) you will need to book a private guide. A Scuba Skills Update
    Refresher Course will be required if anyone in the booking hasn't dived within 12 months.

    ##Weather, Swell and Seasickness Remedies
    Cook Island's position is just south of the often treacherous Tweed River Bar. We

        certification, we can look it up for you, but please request this at least 24 hours
        before diving via email. If no proof of certification can be shown or found on the
        day of diving, we will be unable to take you diving, and no refunds or changes will
        be given.
        Diving Ability, Confidence and Competence: Cook Island Marine Reserve is an open
        ocean dive site that is frequented by all levels of divers; We are unable to predict
        a divers' competence by their qualifications or experience; this varies with every
        individual. However, please be aware that there can be strong swells, strong
        currents, strong surges, cold water and strong winds and it is a requirement that
        divers have the ability, fitness, confidence and competence to dive in such
        conditions. In the winter months, the temperature can drop as low as 19 degrees but
        averages around 22 degrees. If you are unsure about your ability to dive in the
        conditions above, you should book a private guide to look after you. Regular dives
        with Gold Coast Dive Centre are guided group dives, and as such, divers need to have
        the competence, ability and confidence at a level that won't negatively impact the
        group. We do try to group divers according to their experience but this is not always
        possible. If you or anyone in your booking are not a confident diver or there is any
        history of previous problems diving, please also book a private guide to give the
        attention needed. The minimum certification level is Open Water Diver, if you are
        below this certification level (eg: SSI Scuba Diver) you will need to book a private
        guide. A Scuba Skills Update Refresher Course will be required if anyone in the
        booking hasn't dived within 12 months. If no diving in four years or more, then an
        SSI Open Water Course will have to be redone.
        Cook Island Marine Reserve Code of Conduct: Cook Island Marine Reserve is part of the
        NSW National Park. It is an Aquatic Reserve known as Turtle Sanctuary and it is home
        to a permanent population of Sea Turtles, and several threatened or protected
        species. Please follow the Code of Conduct when visiting the Cook Island Waters: no
        touching, collecting, damaging, feeding or moving marine life. Look and keep
        memories, but don’t touch and don’t chase or harass, please be mindful with your
        camera.
        Dive Etiquette: Please give yourself plenty of time to arrive and prepare.
        Good Buddy Behavior and Be self-sufficient.
        Stow your equipment properly.
        Respect Marine Life and Other Divers.
        Be mindful of your position in the water.
        Take only photos, leave only bubbles.
        Use the right rinse bucket.

    [disclaimers] *NEW*
        Personal Items: Gold Coast Dive Centre and its employees take no responsibility for
        personal items or dive gear that are brought onto our property or used during
        activities whether lost, stolen or damaged. With any activity, there is a risk of
        damage to personal gear from handling or normal use. Personal items are brought onto
        the property and stored or used at the owners' own risk. After your activity, please
        double-check that you have everything with you before leaving. If personal items are
        not collected, they will be disposed of after three weeks.

    ##Additional Information
    **Scheduling:** In general camps are 3 days long 9.30-3pm with early morning drop off at
    8.30 onwards and late afternoon pickup until 5pm. Your order will show the start day/time
    for the first day of the camp.
    **Sign-in and out:** Please escort your child/children to the sign in desk at the back of
    Manly Sailing office (end of East Esplanade path) to complete the sign in process. Please
    let staff know if you would like your child to make their own way home and sign the
    appropriate permission slip or email us before hand.
    **Waiver:** Each participant will be required to complete a waiver before participating
    in a course / experience. This can be done [online]
    (https://waiver.smartwaiver.com/w/5d8b0b333d047/web/) or at the office.
    **Location:** Dinghy lessons will start from Manly Sailing. Our office is located on the
    wharf level underneath Many Yacht Club. When in Manly, facing the Manly Ferry Wharf, turn
    left and follow the path around past East Esplanade beach until it ends. A short 10
    minute walk.
    **Food: Please bring recess, lunch and a water bottle** to keep them hydrated and full of
    energy to get through the day. We may stop for lunch at different beaches so please
    ensure they have their food and water ready to go in the morning.
    **Footwear:** Old trainers or wetsuit booties to provide protection from sharp objects.
    **Crocs and Thongs are not permitted** as they cannot be securely fastened to feet.
    Anyone arriving without secure footwear will not be permitted on the boats or the wharf.
    **Hat:** A secure hat that can be tied on is recommended.
    **Shorts:** Shorts over a wetsuit are essential as sailing involves sliding around on the
    boat quite a bit. If you have a wetsuit it is a good idea to bring it.
    **T-Shirt: *A long sleeve rash vest must be worn*** for sun protection and to prevent a
    rash caused by the PFD. Rash vests can be purchased from our office upon arrival.
    **Warm Top:** such as an old polar fleece, or a light wind jacket is advised to add that
    extra layer if it’s chilly.
    **PFD (Personal Floatation Device):** we supply PFD’s for all students. Students may use
    their own but we reserve the right to inspect them and if necessary insist that one of
    ours is worn. Anyone declining to wear their PFD will not be allowed to participate.
    **Sun cream:** Participants should bring their own sun cream, preferably Zinc or at least
    factor 30 or above. Sun cream should be applied at home before attending and during camps
    our staff will supervise reapplication of sun cream at the lunchtime break. If your child
    has allergies to any sunscreens please ensure they have a suitable one packed.
    **Towel:** Participants will get wet during the session so a dry towel for afterwards is
    essential.
    **Secure gear bag:** is required to store all clothes and gear. We will do our best to
    make sure students gear is secure but we do not have lock up facilities so please don’t
    bring valuables. Gear should be labelled clearly to mix-ups / lost property. We will
    store lost property for a maximum of two weeks following an event.
    **Dry clothes:** Participants will get wet during the session so a set of dry clothes for
    afterwards is advised. An old shopping bag is recommended to carry wet gear in is
    recommended.
    **Refunds and changes:** Please see terms and conditions
    **Weather:** Please see terms and conditions

    Kia ora,
    Thank you for booking your place on The Taieri Gorge Stargazer.
    We're delighted to welcome you on board for an evening of dining, rail travel and
    dark-sky discovery within the Taieri Gorge.
    Before your journey, please take a moment to read through the information below.
    ## Check-In & Arrival
    ## Check-In & Arrival
    Please follow the signs to the booking office upon arrival at Dunedin Railway Station.
    * Check-in opens from **4:30pm** and closes at **6:00pm**.
    * Boarding begins at **5:15pm**.
    * All guests must be **checked in, boarded and seated by 5:45pm**.
    * Dinner service will commence at **6:00pm**.
    * The train departs Dunedin Railway Station at **6:30pm**.
    * No need to print your tickets – simply provide your name at check-in.
    We recommend arriving early to enjoy your welcome drink and begin your evening at a
    relaxed pace.
    ## Seating
    Seating is allocated prior to departure.
    Your carriage and seat details will be provided at check-in. If you have a special
    seating request, please contact our booking office at least 48 hours before departure.
    Please note that while we will do our best to accommodate requests, they cannot be
    guaranteed.
    ## Accessibility
    The Stargazer experience includes time spent outdoors at Hindon in low-light conditions
    and may involve uneven ground.
    For this reason, the event is not suitable for guests with significant mobility
    limitations.
    If you have any accessibility questions prior to travel, please contact our team.
    ## Getting to the Station
    You will need to arrange your own transport to Dunedin Railway Station.
    You can find directions and transport information here:
    [Getting Here]
    Parking is available nearby, including pay-and-display parking around the station
    precinct.
    For larger vehicles and campervans, Thomas Burns Street Carpark is recommended.
    [Insert map image]
    ## What to Bring
    Winter evenings in the Taieri Gorge can be cold, so we recommend:
    * Warm layered clothing
    * A jacket suitable for outdoor conditions
    * Closed footwear
    * Hat, scarf and gloves
    * A red-light torch or headlamp (optional)
    * Binoculars or a small telescope (optional)
    To help preserve night vision during stargazing, we ask guests to avoid white-light
    torches where possible.
    ## Food & Drinks
    Your ticket includes:
    * Welcome drink
    * Gourmet dinner served onboard
    * Warm dessert at Hindon
    A selection of additional beverages, including mulled wine and hot chocolate, will be
    available to purchase onboard throughout the evening.
    Dietary requirements advised at the time of booking have been passed on to our catering
    team.
    ## Weather & Stargazing
    The Taieri Gorge Stargazer is designed to operate in a range of winter weather
    conditions.
    If cloud cover limits stargazing opportunities, guests will still enjoy astronomy talks
    from Tūhura Otago Museum, a special astronomy film presented by Winterstellar, and other
    alternative night-sky experiences.
    ## Share Your Journey
    We'd love to see your photos from the evening.
    Tag @DunedinRailStation on social media for a chance to be featured on our channels.
    ## Questions?
    For frequently asked questions, please visit:
    https://dunedinrailwaystation.co.nz/faq/
    If you need assistance before your journey, please contact us:
    [info@dunedinrailways.co.nz](mailto:info@dunedinrailways.co.nz)
    +64 22 436 9074
    We look forward to welcoming you on board for a memorable evening beneath Otago's winter
    skies.
    Ka mihi,
    The Dunedin Railway Station Team
    [info@dunedinrailways.co.nz](mailto:info@dunedinrailways.co.nz) | +64 22 436 9074

    Thank you for booking with us on the NZ International Science Festival 2026's Science
    Train on the Taieri Gorge. We’re so excited to welcome you and your family on board for
    this hands-on science show to Hindon this winter school holidays.
    Here’s everything you need to know before your trip:
    **Check-In is Essential**
    Please follow the signs to the ticket office upon your arrival.
    - Make sure to check in before boarding at the Dunedin Railway Station booking office.
    - Check-in opens one hour before departure. Please board the train at least 20 minutes
    before departure.
    - **No need to print anything** – just let us know your name when you arrive.
    **Seating is Allocated**
    Seating is allocated ahead of time. You will receive your seating information at
    check-in. If you have any special requests, this must be arranged ahead of the day of
    travel. Please call or email our booking office at least 48 hours ahead of time. Please
    be aware, **we cannot guarantee any seating requests.**

    Thank you for your booking, you will receive a seperate email advising pick up times for
    Kuranda and Daintree Rainforest, make own way to the Cairns Marina, Reef Fleet Terminal
    for the Great Barrier Reef Tour
    #Itinerary
    #Day 1 – Great Barrier Reef Tour with Evolution
    - Check-in: 7:15 am at Reef Fleet Terminal, 1 Spence Street, Cairns
    - Operator: Down Under Cruise & Dive
    - Departure: 8:00 am sharp
    - Return: Approximately 4:30 pm
    **Tour Highlights and Inclusions**
    Cruise on board Evolution, a 35-metre luxury superyacht
    5 hours of reef time at two exclusive Outer Reef sites
    Unlimited snorkelling with equipment and flotation devices
    Free lycra/sun suit hire
    Spacious air-conditioned lounges and upper sun deck
    Friendly, qualified crew and instructors
    Inclusions
    BBQ lunch with fresh seafood, steak & salads (vegetarian & GF options available)
    Complimentary glass of wine and snack on return
    Reef levy (included in your package)
    **Not included**
    Return Transfers - additional cost Cairns CBD ($24 per person) and Northern Beaches ($35)
    Please contact us if you wish to include your hotel transfers
    **Diving Information**
    Medical questionnaire required for all divers
    Divers over 65 (or over 45 for PADI courses) must present a “Fit to Dive” medical
    certificate from their GP
    Certain medical conditions or medications may prevent you from diving
    Do not fly within 24 hours after your last dive
    Certified divers must present a valid scuba certification card
    **Dietary Needs**
    Please notify us of any special dietary requirements at least 48 hours before travel
    ##Day 2 - Kuranda Train & SKyrail
    After being picked up from your accommodation, travel to the Skyrail terminal for an
    amazing experience over Australia's World Heritage-listed Tropical Rainforest canopy
    descending into the forest at two stations, Red Peak and Barron Falls Guests can enjoy
    spectacular views from three lookouts at Barron Falls Station and learn more about the
    environment from ranger-guided tours at Red Peak Station.
    Free time in Kuranda the village in the rainforest, with free time to explore the
    markets, shops, and animal attractions and speak with the locals.
    3.30pm Depart on the Kuranda Scenic Train arriving back to Cairns Railway station 5.00pm
    **Make own way back to your chosen accommodation**
    ## Day 3 - Daintree - Cape Tribulation Rainforest Tour with Billy Tea Bush Safaris
    Look out for the “Billy Tea Safaris” vehicle.
    Please be at your pick-up location 5-minutes before your pick-up time to ensure there are
    no delays.
    **Tour Inclusions**
    - 1-hour Daintree River Cruise – spot crocodiles and birdlife
    - Morning tea – tea/coffee and biscuits
    - Cable ferry ride across the Daintree River
    - Scenic stop at Alexandra Lookout
    - Restaurant lunch at Cape Tribulation
    - Guided Elevated Boardwalk Tour – learn about rainforest ecology
    - Beach walk where the Rainforest meets the Reef
    - Tropical Fruit Ice Cream – Signature ice cream cup included
    **Other Information**
    No paper vouchers needed – show confirmation on your phone
    EFTPOS available for onboard purchases
    **Parking Options**
    Council Car Park (across the street): $2.40/hr – coin or payWave accepted
    Pier Underground Car Park: $20/day – pay on exit

    ##FAQ/Important Information
    **MEETING TIME/PLACE ON MORNING OF DEPARTURE:**
    11:00am* @ Coral Sea Marina (South Village Meeting Point C) on the Right-Hand-Side of the
    two buildings.
    Coral Sea Marina was previously known as Abell Point Marina.
    Google Maps link for the meeting point is:
    [https://goo.gl/maps/ouffyb6vfowvKDdt5](https://goo.gl/maps/ouffyb6vfowvKDdt5)
    Be careful not to end up at the North end meeting point.
    *If the departure time changes, you will be notified by email and/or text message. Please
    reply to this email if you have not yet provided both contact types.
    Coral Sea Marina has parking available for $13/day.
    **YOUR ITINERARY:**
    Avatar doesn’t have set itineraries, as we are dependent on weather & tidal conditions.
    When you board Avatar, the crew will go through information specific to the vessel as
    well as where you may be going in the coming days.
    IMPORTANT!
    No large backpacks or suitcases are allowed on-board Avatar. Please only bring bags the
    same size as airline carry-on.
    Most hostel/hotels in Airlie beach have bag storage facilities for bigger bags.
    There is NO bag storage at the marina and you face missing your departure if you bring
    bags that are not allowed.
    **WHAT TO BRING:**
    In a small soft bag (enviro safe), we suggest that you bring the following:
    • Travel voucher from your booking agent.
    • Light Clothing / Warm clothing in cooler months (May - September)
    • Swimsuit
    • Hat
    • Sunscreen (30+ highly recommended)
    • Bath Towel and Beach Towel
    • Sunglasses
    • Insect Repellent
    • Favourite Music
    • Alcohol (no glass please) NO MORE THAN 24 cans of beer OR 4ltrs cask wine OR 1 ltr
    spirits.
    **WHAT NOT TO BRING:**
    • Glass bottles or red wine.
    • Sleeping bags or pillows.
    • Passport or important travel documents
    • Shampoo or conditioner (for environmental purposes)
    • Plastic Bags (They kill our wildlife and smother the coral)
    OzSail is not responsible for any property you take on board the vessel. In particular,
    we strongly encourage you to take waterproof cameras rather than expensive digital
    cameras. Your electrical equipment will be ruined if it comes in contact with salt water.
    **MEALS:**
    If you haven't already confirmed with us about food allergies and/or dietary
    requirements, please call us ASAP to modify your booking.
    All main meals are included. If you love snacks and flavoured drinks (like me), you may
    like to bring some extras including flavoured drinks e.g. orange juice or soft drinks.
    **WEATHER:**
    Welcome to the tropics! Although our winters may be cooler. Our summer months (November
    -March) can be extremely hot and humid, especially downstairs on a boat. Unless you are
    accustomed to living in this climate, you may find it slightly uncomfortable, especially
    at night when you are sleeping. Please be prepared for this.
    **ALCOHOL, SOFT DRINKS AND BOTTLED WATER:**
    An Alcohol policy is in place on Avatar. Each guest can take a maximum of 24 cans of beer
    OR 4ltrs cask wine (goon) OR 1ltr of spirits, any more than this will NOT be allowed
    on-board. All alcohol, soft drinks and bottled water must be purchased prior to boarding
    your vessel. (Please note, we do not allow glass bottles on board)
    **WATER, TEA AND COFFEE:**
    We provide tap water on all our vessels however it isn't cold and some people don't like
    the taste of it. During our summer months, we strongly encourage you to bring bottled
    water. We recommend at least 2 litres per day. Tea and Coffee breaks are generally in the
    morning and afternoon.
    **TRAVEL SICKNESS:**
    If you are not sure whether or not you may suffer from travel sickness, we suggest taking
    travel sickness tablets. Our trained crew will assist as much as possible in making you
    comfortable but they are not allowed to provide you with any medication.
    **SNORKELLING GEAR:**
    Masks and snorkels are all included in the price of your trip and will be distributed at
    the meeting point.
    **LYCRA SUITS & WETSUITS:**
    Wearing a Lycra stinger suit will prevent UV exposure and significantly reduce your risk
    to marine stingers. OzSail; requires that all passengers wear a full-length stinger suit
    or wetsuit if you wish to swim and or snorkel from our vessels.
    You will be fitted at the meeting point and are all inclusive in your ticket price.
    **TRAVEL INSURANCE:**
    We strongly encourage all guests travel with travel insurance with coverage for the
    following situations:
    • Damaged Property (You will be on a boat surrounded by sea water)
    • Medical Emergencies including Ambulance cover and
    • Travel Cancellation & Interruption
    --------------------------------
    Please ensure that you have read all of the above carefully.
    On the date of departure, please ensure you are at Meeting Point C at Coral Sea Marina
    (South Village) before your scheduled departure time. It is critical that the vessel
    leaves on time.
    It will take you 20 mins to walk to Coral Sea Marina from the main street of Airlie
    Beach. If the ocean is on your right-hand side you are walking in the right direction.
    --------------------------------
    **TRAVEL DATES: **
    At the end of your sailing adventure, OzSail have booked you a VIP table at Beaches
    Backpackers at 6:30pm for dinner and drinks followed by free entry and more VIP treatment
    at Paddy's Shenanigans, Airlie's iconic party spot.
    We recommend that you get to Airlie Beach the day before departure and leave Airlie Beach
    the day after you return to land, to enjoy the after party.
    FEEDBACK: OzSail welcomes your honest feedback to help us to improve our trips and levels
    of customer service.
    FROM ALL OF THE STAFF & CREW AT OZSAIL WE HOPE YOU HAVE A WONDERFUL WHITSUNDAY SAILING
    EXPERIENCE!
    ![Description of image](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/ngelWC4FQjiPY0lEmBVg)
    Notice to Passengers on Vessels - Avatar, Mandrake, and Spank Me
    1. AP Vessel Management Pty Ltd trading as OzSail ABN 45 086 439 198.
    2. OzSail operates the vessels Avatar, Mandrake, and Spank Me and is the supplier and

    3. If you have any concerns, queries or require additional information with regards to

    4. OzSail:
    · Website - www.OzSail.com.au
    · Reservations –0499 697 245 OR bookings@ozsail.com.au

    **MEETING TIME/PLACE ON MORNING OF DEPARTURE:**
    08:00AM* @ Coral Sea Marina (South Village Meeting Point C) on the Right-Hand-Side of the
    two buildings.
    Google Maps link for the meeting point is:
    [https://goo.gl/maps/ouffyb6vfowvKDdt5](https://goo.gl/maps/ouffyb6vfowvKDdt5)
    Be careful not to end up at the North end meeting point. Coral Sea Marina was previously
    known as Abell Point Marina.
    *If the departure time changes, you will be notified by email and/or text message. Please
    reply to this email if you have not yet provided both contact types.
    Coral Sea Marina has parking available for $13/day.
    **YOUR ITINERARY:**
    Matador doesn’t have set itineraries, as we are dependent on weather & tidal conditions.
    When you board the vessel, our crew will go through information specific to the vessel as
    well as where you may be going in the coming days.
    **WHEN DO WE RETURN?**
    Every trip is slightly different, but we aim to be back at 16:30 the following day.
    IMPORTANT!
    No large backpacks or suitcases are allowed on-board Matador. Please only bring bags of
    the same size as airline carry-on.
    Most hostel/hotels in Airlie beach have bag storage starting from $5.
    There is NO bag storage at the marina and you face missing your departure if you bring
    bags that are not allowed.
    **WHAT TO BRING:**
    In a small soft bag (enviro safe), we suggest that you bring the following:
    • Travel voucher from your booking agent.
    • Light Clothing / Warm clothing in cooler months (May - September)
    • Swimsuit
    • Hat
    • Sunscreen (30+ highly recommended)
    • Bath Towel and Beach Towel
    • Sunglasses
    • Insect Repellent
    • Favourite Music
    • Alcohol (no glass please) NO MORE THAN 24 cans of beer OR 4ltrs cask wine OR 1 ltr
    spirits.
    **WHAT NOT TO BRING:**
    • Glass bottles or Red Wine.
    • Sleeping bags or pillows.
    • Passport or important Travel Documents
    • Shampoo and Conditioner (for environmental purposes)
    • Plastic Bags (They kill our wildlife and smother the coral)
    Matador Whitsundays is not responsible for any property you take on board the vessel. In
    particular, we strongly encourage you to take waterproof cameras rather than expensive
    digital cameras. Your electrical equipment will be ruined if it comes in contact with
    salt water.
    **MEALS:**
    If you haven't already confirmed with us about food allergies and/or dietary
    requirements, please call us ASAP to modify your booking.
    All main meals are included. If you love snacks and flavoured drinks (like me), you may
    like to bring some extras including flavoured drinks e.g. orange juice or soft drinks.
    **WEATHER:**
    Welcome to the tropics! Although our winters may be cooler. Our summer months (November
    -March) can be extremely hot and humid, especially downstairs on a boat. Unless you are
    accustomed to living in this climate, you may find it slightly uncomfortable, especially
    at night when you are sleeping. Please be prepared for this.
    **ALCOHOL, SOFT DRINKS AND BOTTLED WATER:**
    An Alcohol policy is in place on Matador. Each guest can take a maximum of 24 cans of
    beer OR 4ltrs cask wine (goon) OR 1ltr of spirits, any more than this will NOT be allowed
    on-board. All alcohol, soft drinks and bottled water must be purchased prior to boarding
    your vessel. (Please note, we do not allow glass bottles on board)
    **WATER, TEA AND COFFEE:**
    We provide tap water on all our vessels however it isn't cold and some people don't like
    the taste of it. During our summer months, we strongly encourage you to bring bottled
    water. We recommend at least 2 litres per day. Tea and Coffee breaks are generally in the
    morning and afternoon.
    **TRAVEL SICKNESS:**
    If you are not sure whether or not you may suffer from travel sickness, we suggest taking
    travel sickness tablets. Our trained crew will assist as much as possible in making you
    comfortable but they are not allowed to provide you with any medication.
    **SNORKELLING GEAR:**
    Masks and snorkels are all included in the price of your trip and will be distributed at
    the meeting point.
    **LYCRA SUITS & WETSUITS:**
    Wearing a Lycra stinger suit will prevent UV exposure and significantly reduce your risk
    to marine stingers. Matador requires that all passengers wear a full-length stinger suit
    or wetsuit if you wish to swim and or snorkel from our vessels.
    You will be fitted at the meeting point and are all inclusive in your ticket price.
    **TRAVEL INSURANCE: **
    We strongly encourage all guests travel with travel insurance with coverage for the
    following situations:
    • Damaged Property (You will be on a boat surrounded by sea water)
    • Medical Emergencies including Ambulance cover and
    • Travel Cancellation & Interruption
    --------------------------------
    Please ensure that you have read all of the above carefully.
    On the date of departure, please ensure you are at Meeting Point C at Coral Sea Marina
    (South Village) before your scheduled departure time. It is critical that the vessel
    leaves on time.
    It will take you 20 mins to walk to Coral Sea Marina from the main street of Airlie
    Beach. If the ocean is on your right-hand side you are walking in the right direction.

    [restrictions]
        IMPORTANT!: No large backpacks or suitcases are allowed on-board Spank Me. Please
        only bring bags the same size as airline carry-on. Most hostel/hotels in Airlie beach
        have bag storage facilities for bigger bags. There is NO bag storage at the marina
        and you face missing your departure if you bring bags that are not allowed.
        ALCOHOL, SOFT DRINKS AND BOTTLED WATER: An Alcohol policy is in place on Spank Me.
        Each guest can take a maximum of 24 cans of beer OR 4ltrs cask wine (goon) OR 1ltr of
        spirits, any more than this will NOT be allowed on-board your vessel. All alcohol,
        soft drinks and bottled water must be purchased prior to boarding your vessel.
        (Please note, we do not allow glass bottles on board)
