    Hey There!
    Thanks for booking with us and locking in the date for your Private Tour!
    Now that we have your deposit, Where do we go from here?
    LOCKING THE ITINERARY IN!
    Generally speaking, we have already spoken to you/the customer via email or text and have
    sent some prices and options to you. If you have mentioned exactly which option you
    wanted in your booking form that you just completed then we are immediately booking in
    all of the venues that we've discussed via email/text and you don't need to do anything
    in that regard. It's all been locked in. We will reach out if there are any issues with
    anything.
    If, however you want changes/amendments to what we have spoken about, or if we hadn't
    fully agreed on an itinerary just yet, then please let us know ASAP as we need to get
    things locked in as soon as we can!
    If we haven't spoken at all and you've booked this on your own based on what you've read
    on the website, then we will be reaching out to you shortly to get a gauge on what our
    exact itinerary and prices will be. Note: Prices on our website are more of an indicative
    price if the group is 11 or more people. If you have booked this without speaking to us
    and only have 2-8 people, the prices will be much more (almost double) than what you've
    probably read, so please contact us now so we can get on the same page and send some
    options to you :)
    ROUNDING UP THE TROOPS
    No-one deserves a wine more than you!!! Because unfortunately although you were the
    lovely, well organised and motivated friend/colleague that actually got this wine tour
    booked, it will now be your responsibility to work with us and help round up everyones
    individual payments, finalise numbers, dietary requirements and a pick up address. Here's
    what we are going to need you to do...
    ROUNDING UP PAYMENTS/REMAINING AMOUNT DUE
    In short: You need to collect everyone payments ASAP....
    Assuming that everyone is paying individually, we will be requiring you to collect
    everyones individual payments so that you can send it to us in one payment/transaction 3
    days before the tour start date. Once it is all collected and it is time, we will take
    payment either via bank transfer (preferred) or a payment link which we can send so you
    can pay in one go with a debit/credit card (a good option for anyone with only an
    international bank account/Tourists. Note: the payment link will incur a 2.5% surcharge
    fee which can be quite a lot when you're dealing with big amounts).
    We don't require full payment until 3 DAYS BEFORE THE TOUR. So between then and now its
    your job to collect everyones payments and update us on numbers. We recommend you do this
    sooner than later. In our experience if you give people a chance to flake, they probably
    will! People will say "Yeah, I'm Keen, sign me up" , but then ask them to pay and they go
    silent...So thats why we say get started ASAP, even if its weeks away. This will filter
    out the flakey ones and give us a better idea on numbers early. Please don't consider
    anyone 'confirmed' unless they've ACTUALLY paid you.
    This is important because often we have explained in our original quote that the 'price
    per person' will change based on how many people you have.
    For example, if you were optimistic with numbers thinking you'd have 20 people, and our
    quote said $160 for 16-24 people, but $180 for 12-15 people, and then unfortunately a few
    drop out, then if you end up with 14 people, we will then expect 14 people paying 180$
    basically meaning you are needing to ask for more money from everyone that is
    coming,....in this example....
    So for that reason if you are unsure of how many people will come, we would recommend
    asking people for the higher amount so that you are best prepared for any drop in
    numbers.
    Please keep us posted in particular if there is a serious drop in numbers ...like, as in
    20 down to 10. The numbers 11, 13 and 24 are important to us as those are the max amount
    of seats our vehicles can hold. It helps us organise drivers and vehicles.
    *if this is a corporate event and a company requires an invoice, please let us know who
    we need to address it to and to send it to.
    DIETARY REQUIRMENTS
    Please get a list of any dietary requirements/allergies/vegetarians you have in the
    group. People always assume no-one has any...but if we get a group that has none
    whatsoever, we are shocked. Please do your due diligence and find out if anyone has any
    hidden secret you didn't know about!
    PICK UP ADDRESS
    If you mentioned one in your booking form, that is where we will be assuming we will go.
    If you have a change of heart, let us know. If you didn't put anything and are looking
    for something pretty central, we often find St Pauls cathedral, Flinders street is a good
    central spot for everyone to meet and accessible with buses.
    NEXT CONTACT/HOW TO CONTACT US
    We will send an email that will explain absolutely everything. From your drivers details,
    to the final itinerary and timings, from rules and what to bring, to payment details.
    This normally comes within 10 days of the tour start date. Don't worry, we wont forget to
    do it! That's why it's important you communicate all the above to us as best you can so
    we can make that final email as perfect as possible. We want to know numbers most of all!
    You can email us here at info@teepeetours.com, text on 0423237833 or Whatsapp on
    +61423237833.
    If you have emailed us and we havent responded as quick as you'd like and need some
    instant answers, texting Andrew on 0423237833 or +61423237833 is how you'll get the
    speediest response. From time to time, we have organised your tour so well and ahead of
    time that we put you in the 'easy pile' and sometimes are working with other clients that
    might need a bit more emailing, so do apologise if we are slow! Be pushy if you need to!
    WHEN DO I NEED TO CONFIRM NUMBERS/WHAT IF PEOPLE CANCEL LAST MINUTE
    We understand numbers fluctuate. COVID taught us that. So that's why we dont require full
    payment until 3 DAYS BEFORE TOUR. We feel this gives you more than enough flexibility to
    have numbers drop off. Once payment is made, we generally dont give any refunds. As a
    tour company we are charged based on the numbers we give the venues 2 days before the
    tour. In certain circumstances exceptions can be made, but it can then affect the price
    per oerson for the people who do come. For example if 2 people drop out we 2 days before,
    we mmmmmaaayy give a refund, but it may in turn increase the price per person for those
    that do come.
    Some tour companies ask for full payment weeks before with no or very little refund, so
    this is our way of being flexible. Once its 2 days before the tour, we rarely give any
    refunds.
    CAN WE BRING DRINKS ON THE BUS? DO YOU HAVE AN ESKY/COOLER ON THE BUS?
    We built our tours around having a fun and boozy day out and we always keep that at the
    forefront of our tours. We want you to have a fun time. And we also acknowledge that some
    feel wine tastings are not generous enough to really feel tipsy. We have a bit of a
    common sense approach to our tours. Where we feel, we will always put an extra bottle or
    two on the table if we feel the group needs it. We want you you to feel like you are
    getting your moneys worth. You will generally get 6-7 standard drinks in a space of 4-5
    hours and also have the ability buy as much drink as you want on the day. We aim to be
    the most generous winery tour company in Melbourne. We believe most wine tours are
    operating in a very sleezy and lazy way, but taking your money and finding ways to give
    you as little alcohol as possible. We believe that if we give you lots of wine throughout
    the day, that you'll want to tell your friends about us and it keeps our business alive.
    Because we are so generous, we really need to take your alcohol consumption seriously.
    We NO LONGER ALLOW anyone to bring any drinks on our vehicles whatsoever. Unfortunately
    this is something that is policed quite heavily these days, and where we were once pretty
    lenient, we are no longer. There has been a few drivers in our industry who got caught
    allowing drinking on the buses and the driver themselves were the one that was punished.
    They lost their license as a result. This emphasises that the risk is all on your driver.
    In an ideal world we could pass the punishment onto you and the people drinking, but that
    simply does not happen. It's the driver. Stupid, I know, but those are the rules. And it
    has scared the entire industry. If you are drinking, you don't get in trouble, the driver
    does!
    The simple fact is that it is illegal to drink any alcoholic drinks on any heavy vehicle.
    Every single wine tour is TECHNICALLY breaking the law when allowing drinking on the bus.
    So for that reason we DO NOT ALLOW ALCOHOL ON OUR BUSES. We leave it to the day to apply
    some discretion, but we do not want anyone bringing drinks on the bus to start the day.
    Please do not tell people they can bring drinks, and on that, tell them to NOT bring
    drinks.
    PLEASE CALL ME IF THIS IS AN ISSUE FOR YOU.
    We DO NOT provide coolers/eskys on our buses. You'll need to bring your own.
    CHILDREN/NON DRINKERS?
    Children UNDER 17 come for free. Non Drinkers will get a discount of somewhere between
    30-50$. It's a case by case thing which we will need to communicate via email. When
    children come, we ignore them in the price per person count. If we have 8 adults and 1
    child, we are charging based on 8 adults coming.
    From here on in, good luck with rounding up the payments! It's a bloody hard job
    gathering everyone up! We always try to look after the person like you who is planning it
    all so expect a few free drinks to come your way on the day of the tour!
    Keep us posted!
    Thanks
    Andrew @ Teepee Tours

    # *Our Micro-Grom High Performance Coaching program is for any young surfer U/12 who can
    independently paddle out the back and trim across an unbroken wave. Our programs run for
    3 days:*
    ___________________________________
    ## Rates
    **$399 Per Child for 3 Full Day Intermediate to Advance Camp**
    ___________________________________
    ## Duration
    **6:45am to 4:30pm each day**
    ___________________________________
    ## About
    WHAT IS HIGH PERFORMANCE ALL ABOUT?
    Our high performance coaching camps are about reaching your true surfing ability with the
    help of a few clever strategies, delivered by our highly qualified, professional and
    friendly coaches.
    WHAT STRATEGIES DO YOU USE?
    Video Analysis: We use video analysis to improve your surfing technique and skill level.
    Our high performance coaches film your surfing session from the beach, then sit with you
    to go over your footage in detail and give you constructive feedback on your strengths
    and areas in need of improvement. You then get to go back out in the water to put the
    advice in to practice. You will be amazed at how the slightest tweak can make you look
    and feel like a whole new and improved surfer!
    Surf Skate boards: No wave is ever the same and conditions are forever changing. Practice
    makes improvements and getting the feel of how your body should be balanced and
    positioned is really important to nailing those turns you have always dreamed of! Our
    Surf Skate boards are purpose built to create the same feeling of surfing and let you
    repeatedly practice a manoeuvre (on land) with our high performance coaches right there
    giving instant feedback.
    Competition Practice: This is optional for those participants who are competition
    surfers. If requested, we can hold mock competitions and run through successful heat
    strategies to improve your confidence and technique to be ready for your next comp.
    Strength and Mobility Training: Improve your strength, speed and power through proper
    technique and motivation during our gym sessions. We use gymnastic equipment like
    trampolines and padded mats.
    ___________________________________
    ## Itenerary
    - Customized to suit your ability
    - Local knowledge, local beaches
    - Includes important surf and safety rules
    - Video Analysis
    - Smooth Star & Ramp session
    - Professional and constructive feedback in a relaxed and supportive environment
    - Massive fun!
    *Optional: Get a copy of your footage to play over and over and show family and friends!
    Additional cost of $30*
    ___________________________________
    ## What to Bring
    Please remember the following items:
    - A packed lunch or money to buy lunch at Bakery
    - Swimwear
    - Surfboard (can bring more than one board)
    - Helmet and pads (if have them)
    - Towel
    - Sunscreen
    - Drinking water
    - Beach footwear in summer if the ground is hot
    - Your booking voucher (printed or on your phone)
    - A HUGE smile!!....
    If you would like to use your own wetsuit and surfboard please bring that along too!
    ___________________________________
    ## Inclusions
    We will provide you with the following when you arrive for your camp
    - Sunscreen (if you don't have your own)
    - Skateboards
    - High Performance surf coach from our experienced team.

    WHAT IS HIGH PERFORMANCE ALL ABOUT?
    Our high performance coaching camps are about reaching your true surfing ability with the
    help of a few clever strategies, delivered by our highly qualified, professional and
    friendly coaches.
    WHAT STRATEGIES DO YOU USE?
    Video Analysis: We use video analysis to improve your surfing technique and skill level.
    Our high performance coaches film your surfing session from the beach, then sit with you
    to go over your footage in detail and give you constructive feedback on your strengths
    and areas in need of improvement. You then get to go back out in the water to put the
    advice in to practice. You will be amazed at how the slightest tweak can make you look
    and feel like a whole new and improved surfer!
    Surf Skate boards: No wave is ever the same and conditions are forever changing. Practice
    makes improvements and getting the feel of how your body should be balanced and
    positioned is really important to nailing those turns you have always dreamed of! Our
    Surf Skate boards are purpose built to create the same feeling of surfing and let you
    repeatedly practice a manoeuvre (on land) with our high performance coaches right there
    giving instant feedback.
    Competition Practice: This is optional for those participants who are competition
    surfers. If requested, we can hold mock competitions and run through successful heat
    strategies to improve your confidence and technique to be ready for your next comp.
    Strength and Mobility Training: Improve your strength, speed and power through proper
    technique and motivation during our gym sessions. We use gymnastic equipment like
    trampolines and padded mats.

    # *Our High Performance Coaching program is for young surfers that in school who are
    wanting to improve their surfing technique and maneuvers. Our programs run anywhere from
    4 to 8 weeks each term. We have different surfing squads which cater for our intermediate
    groms, our advanced groms and our state squad.*
    ___________________________________
    ## Rates
    **Full Program:** $70 per week
    **Surfing Training Only:** $60 per week
    **Swimming Squad Only:** $15 per week
    **Strength/Mobility Only:** $15 per week
    ___________________________________
    ## Duration
    Programs change from term to term. They normally run for 4 to 8 weeks per term. Please
    see our term timetable below to see all dates, start time & duration of programs.
    ___________________________________
    ## About
    Our High Performance Grom Squad Term Training sessions are about reaching your true
    surfing ability with our detailed programming and the help of our highly qualified,
    professional and friendly coaches.
    WHAT WE DO
    Surfing: We use video analysis to improve your surfing technique and skill level. Our
    high performance coaches film your surfing session from the beach, then sit with you to
    go over your footage in detail and give you constructive feedback on your strengths and
    areas in need of improvement. You then get to go back out in the water to put the advice
    in to practice. You will be amazed at how the slightest tweak can make you look and feel
    like a whole new and improved surfer! We also hold mock competitions and run through
    successful heat strategies to improve your confidence and technique to be ready for your
    next comp.
    Strength and Mobility Training: Improve your strength, flexibility, speed and power
    through our dynamic and motivating fitness sessions.
    Swimming Squad: We include swimming squad in to our program to enhance groms endurance,
    breathing, paddling power and overall fitness in the water. We keep it exciting by using
    a variety of drills related to styles of surfing and work on sprints, long distance and
    underwater swimming.
    ___________________________________
    ## Itenerary
    - Surfing - maneuvers, heat strategies, video analysis
    - Strengh and mobility training
    - Swimming squad training
    - Professional and constructive feedback in a relaxed and supportive environment
    - Massive fun!
    ___________________________________
    ## What to Bring
    Please remember the following items:
    Surfing:
    - Wetsuit
    - Surfboard
    - Towel
    - Sunscreen
    - Drinking water
    Swimming Squad:
    - Bathers
    - Towel
    - Drinking water
    Strength and Mobility Training:
    - Wetsuit & Surfboard
    - Drinking water
    ___________________________________
    ## Inclusions
    We will provide you with the following when you arrive for your camp
    - Sunscreen (if you dont have your own)
    - Skateboard and helmet for skating session
    - High Performace surf coach from our experienced team.
    ___________________________________
    ## Pickup Information
    Surfing locations are advised the night before via text message.
    Swimming squad is held in our 18m lap pool at 2 Villers St Cowaramup
    Strength and Mobility Training is held at the beach doing surf drill and fitness
    Early Morning Surf Sessions - Parents drop off groms to surf/beach location, we drop
    groms to Margaret River Primary & High School after.
    Afternoon Surf Sessions - We pick up from Margaret River Primary & High School and take
    groms to the beach location for that session. Parents then pick up groms from our house
    at the end.
    Weekend Surf Sesssions - Parents drop off groms at beach location, then pick up their
    groms from our house at the end.

    ##We're thrilled your skydiving with us! Check out the information below to make sure
    you're ready for your adventure of a lifetime.
    If you haven’t already added a media package, you can upgrade on the day OR give us a
    call or email to upgrade and relive the experience forever:
    Personal Photographer
    A personal photographer is a separate skydiver (camera flyer) who jumps with you wearing
    the camera equipment on their helmet. The outside perspective includes full panoramic
    views over the beautiful region, during your free-fall experience. A jumping buddy that
    will capture you pre-jump, and meet you on the ground for a post jump interview.
    Instructor Cam
    Choose to be filmed by your Tandem Master and get up-close shots that will capture every
    expression as you free fall from the plane. This package films the entire skydive
    experience from a close – up wide-angle lens mounted on the Tandem Masters wrist.
    Best of Both Worlds
    Capture the experience of a lifetime from all the best angles with both the Personal
    Photographer and Instructor Cam combined for the most epic memories of your skydive
    experience. Includes photos and videos from both your Tandem Masters camera and a
    separate skydiver (camera flyer) who jumps at the same time as you, wearing the camera
    equipment on their helmet.
    #Check In Time
    For all of our skydives, Please arrive 15 minutes before your selected time for check in.
    #Getting Here
    On Google Maps, navigate to [Skydive Mt. Cook - NZ's Most Spectacular
    Skydive](https://www.google.co.nz/maps/dir//2+Swallow+Drive+Pukaki,+Skydive+Mt.+Cook+-+NZ's+Most+Spectacular+Skydive,+Airport,+Twizel+7999/@-44.2389012,170.1149692,17z/data=!4m9!4m8!1m0!1m5!1m1!1s0x6d2b1f686f5edf1f:0xe48ddb1a1927b34!2m2!1d170.1171579!2d-44.2389051!3e0).
    #Important Information
    - Please fill in the Risk Disclosure attached at the top of this email pre arrival for
    check in.
    - Please allow around 3 hours for the experience, from the time you arrive at the airport
    - If we need to contact you regarding the weather or to reschedule your jump we will
    contact you using the details you provide. If we are unable to rebook you, a full refund
    will be provided.
    - There is a weight limit of 100kg / 220lbs / 15.5 stone for every tandem passenger.
    -Passengers over 100kg may be able to jump, this decision is made individually and on the
    day of the jump, assessment is made by the TMs only. Please let us know before arrival if
    you are over 100kgs.
    - Parental or guardian consent is required for anyone under 18. Children under 12 will be
    evaluated on an individual basis on arrival.
    #What Should You Bring
    - - Closed shoes (without metal lace loops-Lace up Sneakers or Trainers are ideal)
    - Casual/comfortable clothing (add an extra layer during the colder months of the year)
    - A big smile and an epic attitude!
    If you wear any head covering that cannot be removed, please wear the lowest-profile
    option possible. During the gear-up process, you will be fitted with a customer hat and
    goggles, so any head covering may need to be adjusted to ensure a secure and comfortable
    fit under the hat. For safety reasons, please remove any sharp hair accessories, such as
    hairpins, before your skydive.
    #Should you eat?
    In general, it is better to have something in your stomach and eat beforehand. However
    some people may be susceptible to stomach upset and/or motion sickness from all the
    excitement.

    Kia Ora,
    We're looking forward to welcoming you to Camp Epic
    Important info for your stay. Please pass this on to other members of your group.
    ___________________
    ##Check In
    You need to be at Bennett Rd Carpark in Ongarue by 8.30am for your shuttle (or otherwise
    arranged). Please arrive on time for your booking, if you are late it can affect other
    groups that are booked and/or our days logistics. The shuttle may leave without you if
    you are late. The shuttle takes approximately 55-60minutes drive from Ongarue to Pureora.
    ___________________
    ##Itinerary
    Meet us in Ongarue by 8:30am on the morning of Day 1. You and your bike are shuttled from
    Ongarue to Pureora to start your ride. Your luggage and food/beverages are transferred
    from Ongarue direct to Camp Epic. You ride the first 40km of the Timber Trail from
    Pureora to Camp Epic (approx. 5-6 hours). Have a great night's stay at Camp Epic. On day
    2 head out when you're ready to ride the next 42km of the Timber Trail from Camp Epic to
    Ongarue (generally 30-60mins quicker than day 1). Your luggage will be collected and
    transferred back to Ongarue waiting for you from 12pm onwards. When you finish back in
    Ongarue, grab your luggage, pack up, jump in your car home, and we'll see you next time!
    ___________________
    ##The Timber Trail
    The Timber Trail is 82km long and runs from Pureora in the north to Ongarue in the south.
    The Trail is graded easy-intermediate (grade 2-3) and runs along old bush tramlines and
    purpose-built single track. It is important to note the Timber Trail is in back country
    with no escape routes and limited cell reception, be prepared in case something goes
    wrong. A moderate level of fitness is required. The Timber Trail is very well signposted.
    There are kilometre markers every kilometre as well as directional markers whenever there
    is a fork in the track.
    ___________________
    ##What to Bring for your Ride
    You need to be dressed in appropriate gear for a full day of mountain biking in a back
    country area. The weather can be very variable so bring gear for both sunny warm weather
    and for freezing cold wet weather. You will need plenty of water and food for the day.
    Other items to consider are bike repair gear (spare tube, multitool, chain link and chain
    breaker, bike pump), sunscreen, PLB (can be hired from i-sites), first aid kit, camera,
    and change of clothes for after your trip.
    ___________________
    ##Camp Epic Facilities & What to Bring
    Camp Epic is self-catered so you'll need to bring your own food & drinks with you. We
    have cooking facilities so bring something yum to cook so you don't get food envy (don't
    bring freeze-dry meals). You are welcome to bring a chillybin. We do supply breakfast
    that you can help yourself to - tea, instant coffee, milo, uhf milk, bread, cereal (GF
    available), eggs, spreads. Our kitchen /dining area is fully equipped with all the
    cutlery, crockery & utensils needed. To cook we have gas cooktops, a bbq, and a grill
    tripod for over the firepit. There is a fridge for storing goods. Whilst we do have
    recycling bins we'd appreciate if empties were taken back out with you if possible due to
    our isolation from facilities.
    If staying in our canvas tents, all your bedding and towels are provided. If you've
    booked a byo tent site you'll need to bring your own tent, bed, bedding, etc. Our
    ablutions block has flushing toilets & amazing hot showers, just bring your own
    toiletries. We have a fire pit to keep you toastie in the evening (marshmallows
    supplied). Please bring warm clothing and a beanie for the evening as it can get
    extremely cold at night all year round. In our kitchen/dining we have a small collection
    of books, playing cards & board games for your enjoyment. We run on solar power, so power
    is limited, but we do have facilities for charging ebikes & cellphones. Please be
    considerate of other guests and keep noise to a minimum after 10pm. Our Camp Manager
    stays on site so if you need anything during your stay just ask.
    ___________________
    ##Bag Transfers
    Your overnight bags go in a different van to you and your bike. Please ensure you have
    everything you need for your ride packed in a bag with you, and then your overnight gear
    packed in a separate bag to go direct to your accommodation. Please be considerate about
    how much gear you bring as space is often limited in the vans, especially on weekends and
    holidays.
    ___________________
    ##Bike Hire
    If you have booked to hire a bike, please make sure we have your height. Bike hire
    includes the bike, helmet and a bike repair kit. Note bikes do not have panniers, you
    need a backpack. Ensure you have signed the waiver for the bike hire terms & conditions
    above.
    ___________________
    ##Payment
    Please ensure payment is made 1 week prior to your booking. Either by card (credit card
    fee applies) or by bank deposit 03-1322-0775006-00 using your booking number as
    reference. Alternatively you can pay cash/card on arrival if preferred.

    download the directions as there is no mobile coverage in our area. If driving in, the
    road into Camp Epic is on a long and narrow gravel road, please take care. If
    biking/walking in from the Timber Trail, we are located at the 40km marker on the Timber
    Trail.
    ___________________
    ##Facilities
    Camp Epic's glamping accommodation is in canvas tents with twin beds with all bedding and
    towels supplied. If booking a byo tent site you'll need to bring your own tent, bed,
    bedding, etc. Our shared kitchen/dining space is equipped with all the cutlery, crockery
    and utensils needed. For cooking we have gas cooktops, a bbq and a grill tripod for over
    the firepit. There is a fridge to keep your food/drinks cool if required. Our ablutions
    have flushing toilets and the most amazing hot showers. Please bring your own toiletries.
    We have a fire pit to sit by in the evening to stay toastie (marshmallows supplied).
    Please bring warm clothing and a beanie as it can get extremely cold in the evenings all
    year round. In our kitchen/dining we have a small collection of books, playing cards &
    board games for your enjoyment. We run on solar power, so power is limited, but we do
    have facilities for charging ebikes & cellphones. Please be considerate of other guests
    and keep noise to a minimum after 10pm. We have a Camp Manager who stays on site, if you
    need anything during your stay just ask.
    ___________________
    ##Food
    Camp Epic is self-catered, only breakfast is supplied. We have a fully equipped kitchen
    with everything you need to cook your meals. Please bring something yum to cook yourself,
    don't get food envy! You are welcome to bring a chilly-bin with your food/drinks in and
    we do have a fridge. We have a pantry with basic condiments (salt, pepper, oil, etc.).
    For breakfast we supply tea, instant coffee, milo, uhf milk, cereal (GF available),
    bread, spreads and eggs that you can help yourself to. We occasionally stock heat&eat
    meals that are available for an extra charge.
    ___________________
    ##Beverages

    not sell alcohol. Please note that although we have recycling bins we would appreciate if

    Thank you for booking your Fishing Charter with Batemans Bay Fishing. Please note the
    following details and contact us immediately should you have any concerns:
    Departure Time: 7am
    Return Time: 3pm approx.
    Location: Berth C1, Batemans Bay Marina, Beach Road, Batemans Bay
    Parking is near the Raine & Horne real estate building
    It is essential that you arrive at the Marina at least 5‐10 minutes prior to the time
    provided above. If you are late to arrive the Skipper CAN NOT WAIT for you and the
    charter will leave without you. There are no refunds or alternate trips provided if you
    miss your charter because you are late to arrive.
    ****The Charter is strictly non‐smoking and no alcohol to be brought on board*****
    We wish you all the very best of fishing on your charter and should you have any
    questions prior to your day of departure please do not hesitate to contact us on 1800 639
    396. *Should you need to contact the Skipper on the morning of your trip please call 0423
    612 250 between 5am ‐ 6am ONLY.*
    Courtesy Bus available for pick up and drop off, please contact the booking office should
    you require this service.
    M.V. JEAN MARIE
    BATEMANS BAY FISHING
    CANCELLATION POLICY
    CANCELLING YOUR TRIP PRIOR TO DAY OF DEPARTURE
    Payment is required in full upon booking your charter. You may cancel or re‐book for
    another day ONE WEEK PRIOR to the day of your charter without any loss of your monies
    paid. Should you make a cancellation within one week of departure, for any reason, you
    will not receive a refund.
    PRIOR TO DEPARTURE
    If the skipper calls the charter off due to bad weather you will have the option of the\
    next day fishing if possible or if this is not possible a refund of monies paid for your
    fishing.
    If you are out fishing and the skipper calls the charter off within 2 hours of your
    charter, you have the same option of a return trip or refund. If you are out to sea for 2
    hours or more then there is no refund or return trip given.
    If the skipper has doubts about the weather and advises not to go but you wish to go
    anyway there will be no refunds. If you call a charter off and wish to come in early
    there will be no refunds.
    AT SEA
    If you have been at sea for under two hours and the skipper calls the charter off due to
    bad weather you will have the option of the next day fishing if possible or if this is
    not possible a refund of monies paid for your fishing.
    If you have been at sea for more than two hours and either the skipper or all of the
    passengers call the charter off there will be no refunds.
    SEA SICKNESS
    If you call a charter off because of sea sickness there will be no refunds.
    For combined charters where sea sickness occurs, the charter must continue.
    We highly recommend that you seek medical advice and obtain sea sick medication if you
    think you may suffer from sea sickness. The skipper is unable to provide you with any
    medication.
    Returning a passenger to shore due to sea sickness will only occur if the skipper deems
    it necessary. If on combined charters some members are sick and some are not and the
    remainder of the passengers wish to continue with the charter, the skipper may return
    passengers to shore and then go back out to complete the charter. Should this option be
    taken the passengers wishing to return to shore will need to pay additional funds to
    cover the cost of petrol. The cost of such a return journey will depend on the estimated
    fuel usage and the amount will be told to the passengers before the return journey.
    Minimum cost $80.
    WHERE WE FISH
    Your skipper is extremely experienced and is able to provide you the benefits of local
    knowledge. Where we fish also depends on weather conditions and your skipper will take
    you to the appropriate fishing grounds comparable with weather conditions. Distance out
    to sea will also be dependent on weather, current and a variety of sea conditions. Whilst
    every effort is made to catch fish we can not guarantee fish. It is extremely rare that
    you would not catch a fish and you are able to keep what you catch providing that the
    fish are legally able to be kept. Your fish are cleaned, bagged and iced for you to take
    home. We recommend that you have an esky in the car so that you can transport your fish
    home.
    ![Description of image](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/sJXa6f8NTPOmo5AMvkxT)

    # *Our Junior Surf Titles Coaching Squads & Camps is for surfer that have enter the
    Surfing WA Junior Surf Titles in Margaret River, Denmark & Geraldton. We have 3 options
    below*
    ___________________________________
    ## Rates
    **$150 Per Child 1 Day Camp**
    **$299 Per Child 2 Day Camp**
    **$240 Per Child for 4 Week Squad**
    **$300 Per Child for 5 Week Squad**
    ___________________________________
    ## Duration
    Camps & Squads change from term to term. Squad normally run for 4 or 5 weeks & Camps are
    normal 1 or 2 days and run for 7.5 hours each day. Please see our term timetable below to
    see all dates, start time & duration of programs.
    **Term One 2020 Squad & Camp Start:**
    6th March 9:30am to 5pm - Margs Junior Surf Titles Coaching 1 Day Camp
    **Term Two 2020 Squad & Camp Start:**
    27th April - Denmark Junior Surf Titles Coaching Squads 4 weeks
    22nd May 9:30am to 5pm - Denmark Junior Surf Titles Coaching 1 Day Camp
    **Term Four 2020 Squad & Camp Start:**
    28th October - National Junior Titles Development Squads 5 weeks
    29th October - National Junior Titles Development Squads 5 weeks
    **Term One 2021 ** Date coming soon
    _______________________________________
    ## About
    WHAT IS JUNIOR SURF TITLES COACHING SQUADS & CAMPS ALL ABOUT?
    Our high performance coaching camps are about reaching your true surfing ability with the
    help of a few clever strategies, delivered by our highly qualified, professional and
    friendly coaches.
    WHAT STRATEGIES DO YOU USE?
    Video Analysis: We use video analysis to improve your surfing technique and skill level.
    Our high performance coaches film your surfing session from the beach, then sit with you
    to go over your footage in detail and give you constructive feedback on your strengths
    and areas in need of improvement. You then get to go back out in the water to put the
    advice in to practice. You will be amazed at how the slightest tweak can make you look
    and feel like a whole new and improved surfer!
    Competition Practice: We hold mock competitions and run through successful heat
    strategies to improve your confidence and technique to be ready for your next comp.
    Surf Skate boards: No wave is ever the same and conditions are forever changing. Practice
    makes improvements and getting the feel of how your body should be balanced and
    positioned is really important to nailing those turns you have always dreamed of! Our
    Surf Skate boards are purpose built to create the same feeling of surfing and let you
    repeatedly practice a manoeuvre (on land) with our high performance coaches right there

    ##Check in closes 15 minutes prior to departure. Gate closes 5 minutes prior to departure
    time
    ##What to bring
    • Non-slip shoes/boots
    • Waterproof jacket
    • Warm sweater/fleece jacket
    • Sunscreen/ sunglasses
    • Insect repellent
    • Camera/phone
    • Personal medication, including for asthma and allergies
    Cabinet café food and snacks will be available for purchase onboard. Please be aware we
    do not accept cash onboard, please come prepared with a card payment option.
    ##Milford Sound Risk Disclosure
    Visitors to Milford Sound should be aware of various natural hazards when going to
    Milford Sound.
    **Aotearoa New Zealand**
    - Powerful natural forces have shaped Aotearoa New Zealand over millions of years.
    Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of the Pacific Ocean. They
    have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.
    - Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each
    year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage. Understanding
    the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your visit.
    **Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one of the world’s most
    spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep fiord
    have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
    - The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any
    time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes,
    landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    - It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a short
    stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it becomes.
    Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you understand
    the risks, before you go.
    **Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland.
    We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a normal part of
    how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
    Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They
    might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or
    disrupt your visit.
    - Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides.
    These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your
    travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
    - Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But
    they will happen again.
    - The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the
    entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or
    greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this happening in
    the next 50 years (find out more at [af8.org.nz)](https://af8.org.nz/). An earthquake of
    this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.
    **What to do in an earthquake:**
    - DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when
    you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less
    likely you are to be injured.
    - Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers)
    as quickly as possible.

    ##Milford Sound Risk Disclosure
    Visitors to Milford Sound should be aware of various natural hazards when going to
    Milford Sound.
    **Aotearoa New Zealand**
    - Powerful natural forces have shaped Aotearoa New Zealand over millions of years.
    Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of the Pacific Ocean. They
    have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.

    year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage. Understanding
    the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your visit.
    **Piopiotahi Milford Sound**

    spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep fiord
    have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
    - The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any
    time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes,
    landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    - It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a short
    stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it becomes.
    Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you understand
    the risks, before you go.
    **Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland.
    We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a normal part of
    how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
    Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They
    might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or
    disrupt your visit.
    - Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides.
    These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your
    travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
    - Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But
    they will happen again.
    - The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the
    entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or
    greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this happening in
    the next 50 years (find out more at [af8.org.nz)](https://af8.org.nz/). An earthquake of
    this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.
    **What to do in an earthquake:**
    - DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when
    you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less
    likely you are to be injured.
    - Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers)
    as quickly as possible.
    **Landslides at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - steep mountains around Piopiotahi Milford Sound are prone to rockfall and landslides.
    Earthquakes and severe weather can make the cliffs unstable, sending rock and debris down
    at speed.
    - Smaller rockfalls are common but often go unnoticed, unless you are nearby.
    - Bigger landslides do not happen often. The chance of one occurring during a short visit
    is extremely unlikely. However, they could cause a tsunami in the fiord and do pose a
    risk to life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    - Large earthquakes are the most common trigger of big landslides in Fiordland. A large
    earthquake during your visit is extremely unlikely, especially for a short stay.
    **Be prepared for landslides**
    - Take extra supplies, food, water, first aid, clothes in your vehicle when travelling in
    remote areas, in case you get stuck – The road from Te Anau to Piopiotahi Milford Sound,
    is prone to avalanches, rockfall and landslides. It is monitored 24/7 by the Milford Road
    Alliance. However, if you get stuck, it will take time for help to reach you. Having
    extra supplies in your vehicle will make the wait time more comfortable.
    - If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust clouds, loud rumbling, or
    splashing. Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord
    and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    **Tsunami at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Like all of Aotearoa New Zealand’s coastline, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is at risk of
    tsunami from multiple sources.
    - The most common threat comes from distant earthquakes in the Pacific Ocean. These
    ocean-source tsunamis take hours to reach our shores. Official warnings are issued in
    time for people to move to safety.
    - Less common, but of more concern, is the potential for a large landslide to fall into
    the fiord and trigger a tsunami.
    - Landslide-triggered tsunamis are rare. The chance of one occurring during your visit is
    extremely unlikely. However, they can create large waves and do pose a risk to life at
    Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    **Be prepared for tsunamis**
    - Triggered by an earthquake – If you feel a LONG (1 minute or more) or STRONG (cannot
    stand up) earthquake, while at Piopiotahi Milford Sound, Get GONE. Move up and away from
    waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    - Triggered by a landslide – If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust
    clouds, loud rumbling, splashing or unusual water behavior, GET GONE. Move up and away
    from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    **Plans and preparedness**
    - Piopiotahi Milford Sound has emergency response plans. These coordinate multiple
    agencies in a State or Emergency. The plans cover earthquakes, tsunami, landslides,
    avalanches, flooding, severe weather and other emergencies.
    - All tourism operators maintain their own emergency procedures. These integrate with the
    wider response in a State of Emergency.
    - If a large landslide triggers a tsunami, there will be no warning. Emergency support
    will take time to arrive. Visitors and workers should be aware of the risk to life and
    prepared to move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as
    possible.
    For more detailed information, please visit [Emergency Management
    Southland](https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or
    [AF8](https://af8.org.nz/).
    **Contact Us**
    For enquiries about your reservation, please contact the RealNZ team on
    [contact@realnz.com](mailto:contact@realnz.com) or [0800 65 65 01](tel:08006565010). For
    transport enquiries within 24 hours of your departure, please contact Altitude Tours on

        Tsunami at Piopiotahi Milford Sound:
        Like all of Aotearoa New Zealand’s coastline, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is at risk of
        tsunami from multiple sources.
        The most common threat comes from distant earthquakes in the Pacific Ocean. These
        ocean-source tsunamis take hours to reach our shores. Official warnings are issued in
        time for people to move to safety.
        Less common, but of more concern, is the potential for a large landslide to fall into
        the fiord and trigger a tsunami.
        Landslide-triggered tsunamis are rare. The chance of one occurring during your visit
        is extremely unlikely. However, they can create large waves and do pose a risk to
        life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
        Be prepared for tsunamis:
        Triggered by an earthquake – If you feel a LONG (1 minute or more) or STRONG (cannot
        stand up) earthquake, while at Piopiotahi Milford Sound, Get GONE. Move up and away
        from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
        Triggered by a landslide – If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust
        clouds, loud rumbling, splashing or unusual water behavior, GET GONE. Move up and
        away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
        Plans and preparedness:
        Piopiotahi Milford Sound has emergency response plans. These coordinate multiple
        agencies in a State or Emergency. The plans cover earthquakes, tsunami, landslides,
        avalanches, flooding, severe weather and other emergencies.
        All tourism operators maintain their own emergency procedures. These integrate with
        the wider response in a State of Emergency.
        If a large landslide triggers a tsunami, there will be no warning. Emergency support
        will take time to arrive. Visitors and workers should be aware of the risk to life
        and prepared to move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as
        possible.
        For more detailed information, please visit Emergency Management Southland
        (https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or AF8
        (https://af8.org.nz/).

        For transport enquiries within 24 hours of your departure, please contact Altitude

    ##If joining this tour from our Visitor Centre, please check-in 15 minutes before your
    departure
    ##Includes return journey back to Queenstown
    ##Taxi pickups may be offered for guests staying at selected accommodations. Please note
    taxis are not included for drop off when the tour returns.
    ##What to bring
    • Non-slip shoes/boots
    • Waterproof jacket
    • Warm sweater/fleece jacket
    • Sunscreen/ sunglasses
    • Insect repellent
    • Camera/phone
    • Personal medication, including for asthma and allergies
    • If booking includes an infant, guests are welcome to bring their own car seat if they
    wish
    Drinks and snacks are available for purchase. This is a cashless experience so please
    come prepared.
    ##Milford Sound Risk Disclosure
    Visitors to Milford Sound should be aware of various natural hazards when going to
    Milford Sound.
    **Aotearoa New Zealand**
    - Powerful natural forces have shaped Aotearoa New Zealand over millions of years.
    Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of the Pacific Ocean. They
    have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.
    - Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each
    year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage. Understanding
    the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your visit.
    **Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one of the world’s most
    spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep fiord
    have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
    - The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any
    time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes,
    landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    - It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a short
    stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it becomes.
    Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you understand
    the risks, before you go.
    **Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland.
    We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a normal part of
    how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
    Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They
    might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or
    disrupt your visit.
    - Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides.
    These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your
    travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
    - Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But
    they will happen again.
    - The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the
    entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or
    greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this happening in
    the next 50 years (find out more at [af8.org.nz)](https://af8.org.nz/). An earthquake of
    this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.
    **What to do in an earthquake:**
    - DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when
    you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less
    likely you are to be injured.
    - Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers)
    as quickly as possible.
    **Landslides at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - steep mountains around Piopiotahi Milford Sound are prone to rockfall and landslides.
    Earthquakes and severe weather can make the cliffs unstable, sending rock and debris down
    at speed.
    - Smaller rockfalls are common but often go unnoticed, unless you are nearby.
    - Bigger landslides do not happen often. The chance of one occurring during a short visit
    is extremely unlikely. However, they could cause a tsunami in the fiord and do pose a
    risk to life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    - Large earthquakes are the most common trigger of big landslides in Fiordland. A large
    earthquake during your visit is extremely unlikely, especially for a short stay.
    **Be prepared for landslides**
    - Take extra supplies, food, water, first aid, clothes in your vehicle when travelling in
    remote areas, in case you get stuck – The road from Te Anau to Piopiotahi Milford Sound,
    is prone to avalanches, rockfall and landslides. It is monitored 24/7 by the Milford Road
    Alliance. However, if you get stuck, it will take time for help to reach you. Having
    extra supplies in your vehicle will make the wait time more comfortable.
    - If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust clouds, loud rumbling, or
    splashing. Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord
    and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    **Tsunami at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Like all of Aotearoa New Zealand’s coastline, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is at risk of
    tsunami from multiple sources.
    - The most common threat comes from distant earthquakes in the Pacific Ocean. These
    ocean-source tsunamis take hours to reach our shores. Official warnings are issued in
    time for people to move to safety.
    - Less common, but of more concern, is the potential for a large landslide to fall into
    the fiord and trigger a tsunami.
    - Landslide-triggered tsunamis are rare. The chance of one occurring during your visit is
    extremely unlikely. However, they can create large waves and do pose a risk to life at
    Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    **Be prepared for tsunamis**
    - Triggered by an earthquake – If you feel a LONG (1 minute or more) or STRONG (cannot
    stand up) earthquake, while at Piopiotahi Milford Sound, Get GONE. Move up and away from
    waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    - Triggered by a landslide – If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust
    clouds, loud rumbling, splashing or unusual water behavior, GET GONE. Move up and away
    from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    **Plans and preparedness**
    - Piopiotahi Milford Sound has emergency response plans. These coordinate multiple
    agencies in a State or Emergency. The plans cover earthquakes, tsunami, landslides,
    avalanches, flooding, severe weather and other emergencies.
    - All tourism operators maintain their own emergency procedures. These integrate with the
    wider response in a State of Emergency.
    - If a large landslide triggers a tsunami, there will be no warning. Emergency support
    will take time to arrive. Visitors and workers should be aware of the risk to life and
    prepared to move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as
    possible.
    For more detailed information, please visit [Emergency Management
    Southland](https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or
    [AF8](https://af8.org.nz/).

        happening in the next 50 years (find out more at af8.org.nz) (https://af8.org.nz/).
        An earthquake of this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and
        surrounding area.
        What to do in an earthquake: DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries
        from earthquakes happen when you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the
        ground/floor you are, the less likely you are to be injured.
        Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and
        rivers) as quickly as possible.
        Landslides at Piopiotahi Milford Sound: steep mountains around Piopiotahi Milford
        Sound are prone to rockfall and landslides. Earthquakes and severe weather can make
        the cliffs unstable, sending rock and debris down at speed.
        Smaller rockfalls are common but often go unnoticed, unless you are nearby.
        Bigger landslides do not happen often. The chance of one occurring during a short
        visit is extremely unlikely. However, they could cause a tsunami in the fiord and do
        pose a risk to life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
        Large earthquakes are the most common trigger of big landslides in Fiordland. A large
        earthquake during your visit is extremely unlikely, especially for a short stay.
        Be prepared for landslides: Take extra supplies, food, water, first aid, clothes in
        your vehicle when travelling in remote areas, in case you get stuck – The road from
        Te Anau to Piopiotahi Milford Sound, is prone to avalanches, rockfall and landslides.
        It is monitored 24/7 by the Milford Road Alliance. However, if you get stuck, it will
        take time for help to reach you. Having extra supplies in your vehicle will make the
        wait time more comfortable.
        If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust clouds, loud rumbling, or
        splashing. Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the
        fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
        Tsunami at Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Like all of Aotearoa New Zealand’s coastline,
        Piopiotahi Milford Sound is at risk of tsunami from multiple sources.
        The most common threat comes from distant earthquakes in the Pacific Ocean. These
        ocean-source tsunamis take hours to reach our shores. Official warnings are issued in
        time for people to move to safety.
        Less common, but of more concern, is the potential for a large landslide to fall into
        the fiord and trigger a tsunami.
        Landslide-triggered tsunamis are rare. The chance of one occurring during your visit
        is extremely unlikely. However, they can create large waves and do pose a risk to
        life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
        Be prepared for tsunamis: Triggered by an earthquake – If you feel a LONG (1 minute
        or more) or STRONG (cannot stand up) earthquake, while at Piopiotahi Milford Sound,
        Get GONE. Move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as
        possible.
        Triggered by a landslide – If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust
        clouds, loud rumbling, splashing or unusual water behavior, GET GONE. Move up and
        away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
        Plans and preparedness: Piopiotahi Milford Sound has emergency response plans. These
        coordinate multiple agencies in a State or Emergency. The plans cover earthquakes,
        tsunami, landslides, avalanches, flooding, severe weather and other emergencies.
        All tourism operators maintain their own emergency procedures. These integrate with
        the wider response in a State of Emergency.
        If a large landslide triggers a tsunami, there will be no warning. Emergency support
        will take time to arrive. Visitors and workers should be aware of the risk to life
        and prepared to move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as
        possible.
        For more detailed information, please visit Emergency Management Southland
        (https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or AF8
        (https://af8.org.nz/).

    ## Thank You for Booking with Canyoning New Zealand!
    We're excited to welcome you on our **Gibbston Valley Half Day Adventure** and can't wait
    to share one of New Zealand’s most spectacular wilderness experiences with you.
    ## Before Your Adventure
    ### Meeting Location & Parking
    **Queenstown Pick-Up – 08:20am and 01.20pm meeting time**
    Please wait outside the Eichardt’s Hotel.
    **Address:** 2 Marine Parade, Queenstown 9300
    [Google Maps Pin](https://maps.app.goo.gl/pK9XELRkRrU83L1Z8)
    Please note that parking is not available at the Queenstown pick-up location. If you are
    driving, please allow extra time to find parking nearby and walk to the meeting point
    before your scheduled check-in time.
    Central Queenstown Parking Suggestion
    **Address:** 10 Boundary Street, Queenstown 9300
    [Google Maps Pin](https://maps.app.goo.gl/wCbBz8Pn6U2zLY1i9)
    ### Important: Please Arrive on Time
    Our guides begin preparing the group as soon as check-in opens to ensure a safe and
    timely departure. As we operate multiple tours each day and need to respect the schedules
    of all guests, we are unable to delay departures for late arrivals.
    ### What to Bring
    Please bring:
    * Swimwear to wear under your wetsuit
    * A towel for after the adventure
    * A personal water bottle
    * Any personal medications you may require
    For your peace of mind, we recommend leaving unnecessary valuables at home.
    Your dry clothes and personal belongings can be stored in our lock box while you are in
    the canyon. While we have never experienced any security issues, we still recommend
    bringing only what you need for the adventure.
    ### Lunch is included on the 08.30am tour
    Participants will receive a lunch voucher to enjoy at one of our selected Queenstown
    partner restaurants.
    **[Erik's Fish and Chips](https://www.eriks.nz/)**
    **[Sushi
    Box](https://www.google.com/search?sca_esv=0b1c7d926c8058f9&sxsrf=ANbL-n5yt_m7-kDNKzQGOA6U2YaJliWBXQ:1781738093717&kgmid=/g/11c5qr7scr&q=Sushi+Box&shem=epsd1,ltac,rimspwouoe&shndl=30&source=sh/x/loc/uni/m1/1&kgs=bb89175a1f5b8d52&utm_source=epsd1,ltac,rimspwouoe,sh/x/loc/uni/m1/1)**
    **[Balls and Bangles](https://www.ballsandbangles.com/)**
    ### Important Safety Information
    Please take the time to review our risk acknowledgement Information before your
    adventure:
    **[Please Read](https://www.canyoningnewzealand.co.nz/safety/)**
    Please contact us before your tour if you have any injuries, medical conditions, or
    concerns about your suitability for the activity. Please also note that all bookings are
    subject to our 48-hour cancellation policy.
    ### Need Assistance?
    Our friendly reservations team is here to help.
    **Phone:** +64 3 428 0071
    **Open daily:** 8:00am – 8:00pm
    ### Tiaki Promise
    New Zealand is a truly special place, and everyone who lives here or visits has a
    responsibility to help protect it. The Tiaki Promise is a commitment to care for
    Aotearoa, now and for future generations.
    By embracing the Tiaki Promise, you are choosing to act as a guardian — respecting the
    land, protecting the environment, and preserving the natural beauty we are privileged to
    explore.
    **Nau mai, haere mai ki Aotearoa — Welcome to New Zealand!**
    **[Learn more](https://www.tiakinewzealand.com/en_NZ/)**
    ### Help Keep New Zealand Wild
    We're committed to reducing our environmental impact and offsetting our carbon footprint
    by planting native trees throughout the Wakatipu region.

    ## Thank You for Booking with Canyoning New Zealand!
    We're excited to welcome you on our **Gibbston Valley 3hr Self Drive Adventure** and
    can't wait to share one of New Zealand’s most spectacular wilderness experiences with
    you.
    ## Before Your Adventure
    ### Arriving at Gibbston Valley
    As you are self-driving to Gibbston Valley, please allow plenty of time before your
    scheduled check-in to use the public toilets, park your vehicle, and walk to our meeting
    point. We recommend arriving at least 10–15 minutes early so you're ready to check in and
    begin your adventure on time.
    ### Public Toilets
    We recommend using the public toilets before checking in. They are located approximately
    100 metres along Coalpit Road from State Highway 6.
    **Public Toilets Address:** Coalpit Road, Gibbston Valley 9371
    [**Google Maps Pin** ](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ByEnPXx8ShQ4iwucA)
    ### Public Parking
    Please park your vehicle in the public parking area located just off State Highway 6
    beside the historic stone hut building.
    To help ensure a smooth start to your adventure, please **do not park in the Gibbston
    Tavern car park**, as it is reserved for Tavern customers. Parking there may require you
    to move your vehicle, which could cause you to miss your scheduled check-in.
    **Public Parking Address:** Coalpit Road, Gibbston Valley 9371
    [**Google Maps Pin** ]( https://maps.app.goo.gl/Cfnk3QVCJaBpRcTD9)
    ### Check-In Location
    From the parking area, it's just a short 2-minute walk to our check-in location. Please
    make your way to the Canyoning New Zealand branded changing shelter, located at the far
    end of the Gibbston Tavern car park.
    Your guides will meet you at the shelter for check-in and help you get ready for your
    adventure. If you arrive early, please wait at the shelter and we’ll be with you shortly.
    **Gibbston Valley Changing Shelter Check In – 09:00am and 02.00pm meeting time**
    **Address:** 8 Coalpit Road, Gibbston Valley 9371
    [**Google Maps Pin** ](https://maps.app.goo.gl/hs1a2zTBDGGu82np7)
    ### Important: Please Arrive on Time
    Our guides begin preparing the group for departure as soon as check-in starts. If you
    arrive after your scheduled check-in time, you may be considered to have missed your
    tour, even if our team is still at the changing shelter.
    To ensure a smooth start for everyone, please arrive on time and allow plenty of time for
    parking, using the public toilets, and walking to the check-in location.
    ### What to Bring
    Please bring:
    * Swimwear to wear under your wetsuit
    * A towel for after the adventure
    * A personal water bottle
    * Any snacks or food you may require
    * Any personal medications you may require
    For your peace of mind, we recommend leaving unnecessary valuables at home or in your
    personal vehicle.
    Your dry clothes and personal belongings can be stored in our lock box while you are in
    the canyon. While we have never experienced any security issues, we still recommend
    bringing only what you need for the adventure.
    ### Important Safety Information
    Please take the time to review our risk acknowledgement Information before your
    adventure:
    **[Please Read](https://www.canyoningnewzealand.co.nz/safety/)**
    Please contact us before your tour if you have any injuries, medical conditions, or
    concerns about your suitability for the activity. Please also note that all bookings are
    subject to our 48-hour cancellation policy.
    ### Need Assistance?
    Our friendly reservations team is here to help.
    **Phone:** +64 3 428 0071
    **Open daily:** 8:00am – 8:00pm
    ## Tiaki Promise
    New Zealand is a truly special place, and everyone who lives here or visits has a
    responsibility to help protect it. The Tiaki Promise is a commitment to care for
    Aotearoa, now and for future generations.
    By embracing the Tiaki Promise, you are choosing to act as a guardian — respecting the
    land, protecting the environment, and preserving the natural beauty we are privileged to
    explore.
    **Nau mai, haere mai ki Aotearoa — Welcome to New Zealand!**
    **[Learn more](https://www.tiakinewzealand.com/en_NZ/)**
    ### Help Keep New Zealand Wild
    We're committed to reducing our environmental impact and offsetting our carbon footprint
    by planting native trees throughout the Wakatipu region.
    If you'd like to support this initiative, you can make a voluntary $5 contribution here:
    **[Donate
    Now](https://fareharbor.com/embeds/book/canyoningnewzealand/items/387858/calendar/?flow=489300&full-items=yes)**
    Thank you for choosing Canyoning New Zealand. We look forward to sharing an unforgettable
    day of adventure, wilderness and incredible scenery with you.
    See you soon!

    You are not required to hire your snow gear or equipment at the first rental stop.

    The coach doors will remain closed after drop-off

    “No Waiting” policy. In an event that any of our passengers are late or fails to board

    **Fare Conditions**
    All fares are subject to change without prior notice.
    Adult fare applies to passengers aged 14 years and above.
    Passengers aged 14–17 years must travel with an accompanying adult aged 18 or above.
    Child fare applies to passengers aged 13 years and under.

    operational changes.

    conditions.
    Allocated seating is not available. Seating is based on first come first served basis.
    **Food & Beverages**
    Light snacks and cold food are permitted onboard.
    Hot food and hot drinks are not permitted due to strong odours and safety considerations.
    Non-alcoholic beverages are allowed.
    Glass bottles are strictly prohibited onboard the coach.
    Alcohol consumption is not permitted onboard.
    **Passenger Behaviour**
    Brighton Tours reserves the right to refuse boarding or remove any passenger who:

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  RAW BOOKING NOTES
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Your booking for the Light Meter Workshop is confirmed. Please aim to arrive at least 5
    minutes early.
    #**What is correct exposure and using a light meter workshop**
    **Highlights:**
    What you will learn is how correct exposure is defined and how to look, expose and shoot
    for it, to obtain consistent correct exposures time and time again. And how correct
    exposure forms the foundation of a good photograph. Develop an understanding of how
    different light meters work in incident, reflected and flash & when you should use one.
    How to define and look for blacks, whites, tonal ranges, detail in highlight and shadow.
    Includes grey, B&W & colour scales & passport checker.
    **What’s Included:**
    • 2 hours training with an award-winning professional photographer of 36 years.
    • Individual assistance in a group of 4 or less
    • Feedback and shooting tips
    • Practical exercises in exposure in a professional studio
    • Light meters of differing types, B&W scales, colour scales & passport checker.
    • Photography notes
    **Session Length:**
    This course runs for 2 hours from 6pm – 8pm
    **Format:**
    This will consist of a brief lecture on basic light metering, followed by a short
    practical session in the studio for assessment and critique of photographs taken.
    **Important information:**
    **What to bring:**
    On the day bring your digital SLR camera body and close to standard lens with charged
    batteries, CF or SD card, whichever card your camera takes and your camera instruction
    book plus a notepad and pen.
    **Numbers on the day:**
    This workshop runs with a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 4
    **Weather:**
    This workshop will be run in a professional studio indoors.
    **Dress code:**
    Casual comfortable clothes
    **Location:**
    The experience takes place bayside in Melbourne at a professional studio.

  RAW BOOKING NOTES
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Your booking for the Develop and Scan Workshop is confirmed. Please aim to arrive at
    least 5 minutes early.
    #**Shoot, Develop & Scan B&W 35mm film**
    **Highlights:**
    You will be given a roll of 35mm B&W film to go into your camera, followed by a shooting
    task. A lecture on film processing and then in a 1 on 1 learning environment you will
    learn how to process your own film, assess it for correct exposure on a light table,
    sleeve it, and then scan the images to be able to take home on a thumb drive you supply.
    **What’s Included:**
    • 4 hours training with an award-winning professional photographer of 36 years.
    • 1 on 1 instruction
    • Feedback and shooting tips
    • Practical exercises in exposure in a professional studio
    • 35mm B&W film, chemistry, darkroom, light table neg sleeves, scanner software, and
    computers.
    • Photography notes
    **Session Length:**
    This course runs for 4 hours from 12pm – 4pm
    **Format:**
    This will consist of a brief lecture on basic light metering, followed by a short
    practical session in the studio for assessment and critique of photographs taken.
    **Prerequisite:**
    Must have completed the Light meter course prior to commencing this one.
    **Important information:**
    **What to bring:**
    On the day bring your 35mm film SLR camera body and close to 50 mm. standard lens with
    charged batteries, and your camera instruction book plus a notepad and pen. Bring a USB
    2.0 thumb drive to take your scanned images home again on.
    **Numbers on the day:**
    This workshop operates 1 on 1.
    **Weather:**
    This workshop will be run in a professional studio indoors.
    **Dress code:**
    Casual comfortable clothes, dust jacket, or overalls type clothing as we will be working
    with chemistry in a darkroom.
    **Location:**
    The experience takes place bayside in Melbourne at a professional studio with free
    off-the-street parking.

    #WEATHER CHECK – ESSENTIAL INFORMATION
    ##You will be advised the day prior of meeting time and confirmation of the flight.
    Please be ready on time, late arrivals may miss the balloon.
    ##Weather Conditions
    Safety is always our primary concern. In the unfortunate event that your flight has to be
    cancelled it is for a genuine reason. We do not take risks with the weather. Your flight
    booking is valid for 12 months from purchase (unless otherwise stipulated) and we can
    always try again another day!
    ##Cancellations
    If you cancel within 72 hours of departure or do not show up on the morning you will not
    be given a refund.
    ##WHEN AND WHERE WE MEET
    We meet in the front foyer of the **Hyatt Hotel**, 120 Commonwealth Ave, Yarralumla, **at
    5.45am**.
    *Please be on time, late arrivals may miss the balloon.* If you are lost or running late
    please phone +61 2 6249 8660.
    Please note parking charges do apply Tuesday to Friday during regular office hours.
    After the flight we celebrate with some Australian sparkling wine and fruit juice. We
    then return to the Hyatt. Plan to be with us for approximately 3 to 4 hours.
    ##WHAT TO WEAR AND BRING
    Wear comfortable clothes as for hiking, i.e. long pants and sturdy shoes that will keep
    your feet warm and dry in the wet grass (not high heels or sandals).
    It will not be any colder in the air than on the ground. Dress in layers, so that you can
    take a jacket or jumper off, so as not to become too warm in the balloon. We suggest you
    bring a cap as it can get warm on your head, underneath the 'burner'. Sunglasses are also
    recommended.
    Bring your camera this is a really fantastic photo opportunity. Personal belongings are
    taken on board at your own risk and should be kept to a minimum.
    Be aware **YOU WILL BE CLOSE TO OTHER PASSENGERS** during your outdoor adventure.
    ##Fit to Fly
    Ballooning can involve some active participation and as such, a moderate level of fitness
    and wellbeing is required.
    All members of your party will need to be fit & well with:
    - No significant knee problems,
    - No significant hip problems,
    - No significant back or neck problems,
    - No recent surgeries or broken bones,
    - No other existing conditions that would preclude from following the Pilot's
    instructions; Assuming the landing position with knees bent when instructed to do so,
    Absorbing a small bump when the balloon is landing or would prevent them from holding on
    to the safety handles when the balloon is landing,
    - Are able to stand for one hour un-assisted,
    - Do not weight more than 140kg individually and Children do not weigh more than 50kg
    individually,
    - Are not Pregnant
    ![Description of image](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/4EnAwWPxQEWnpPYwNY7W)
    ##If you have any concerns about your fitness to fly, or any other questions, please call
    02 6248 8200 to discuss.
