    Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of the Pacific Ocean. They
    have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.
    - Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each
    year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage. Understanding
    the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your visit.
    **Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one of the world’s most
    spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep fiord
    have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
    - The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any
    time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes,
    landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    - It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a short
    stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it becomes.
    Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you understand
    the risks, before you go.
    **Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland.
    We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a normal part of
    how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
    Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They
    might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or
    disrupt your visit.
    - Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides.
    These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your
    travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
    - Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But
    they will happen again.
    - The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the
    entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or
    greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this happening in
    the next 50 years (find out more at [af8.org.nz)](https://af8.org.nz/). An earthquake of
    this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.
    **What to do in an earthquake:**
    - DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when
    you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less
    likely you are to be injured.
    - Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers)
    as quickly as possible.
    **Landslides at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - steep mountains around Piopiotahi Milford Sound are prone to rockfall and landslides.
    Earthquakes and severe weather can make the cliffs unstable, sending rock and debris down
    at speed.
    - Smaller rockfalls are common but often go unnoticed, unless you are nearby.
    - Bigger landslides do not happen often. The chance of one occurring during a short visit
    is extremely unlikely. However, they could cause a tsunami in the fiord and do pose a
    risk to life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    - Large earthquakes are the most common trigger of big landslides in Fiordland. A large
    earthquake during your visit is extremely unlikely, especially for a short stay.
    **Be prepared for landslides**
    - Take extra supplies, food, water, first aid, clothes in your vehicle when travelling in
    remote areas, in case you get stuck – The road from Te Anau to Piopiotahi Milford Sound,
    is prone to avalanches, rockfall and landslides. It is monitored 24/7 by the Milford Road
    Alliance. However, if you get stuck, it will take time for help to reach you. Having
    extra supplies in your vehicle will make the wait time more comfortable.
    - If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust clouds, loud rumbling, or
    splashing. Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord
    and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    **Tsunami at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Like all of Aotearoa New Zealand’s coastline, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is at risk of
    tsunami from multiple sources.
    - The most common threat comes from distant earthquakes in the Pacific Ocean. These
    ocean-source tsunamis take hours to reach our shores. Official warnings are issued in
    time for people to move to safety.
    - Less common, but of more concern, is the potential for a large landslide to fall into
    the fiord and trigger a tsunami.
    - Landslide-triggered tsunamis are rare. The chance of one occurring during your visit is
    extremely unlikely. However, they can create large waves and do pose a risk to life at
    Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    **Be prepared for tsunamis**
    - Triggered by an earthquake – If you feel a LONG (1 minute or more) or STRONG (cannot
    stand up) earthquake, while at Piopiotahi Milford Sound, Get GONE. Move up and away from
    waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    - Triggered by a landslide – If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust
    clouds, loud rumbling, splashing or unusual water behavior, GET GONE. Move up and away
    from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    **Plans and preparedness**
    - Piopiotahi Milford Sound has emergency response plans. These coordinate multiple
    agencies in a State or Emergency. The plans cover earthquakes, tsunami, landslides,
    avalanches, flooding, severe weather and other emergencies.
    - All tourism operators maintain their own emergency procedures. These integrate with the
    wider response in a State of Emergency.
    - If a large landslide triggers a tsunami, there will be no warning. Emergency support
    will take time to arrive. Visitors and workers should be aware of the risk to life and
    prepared to move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as
    possible.
    For more detailed information, please visit [Emergency Management
    Southland](https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or
    [AF8](https://af8.org.nz/).
    **Contact Us**
    For enquiries about your reservation, please contact the RealNZ team on
    [contact@realnz.com](mailto:contact@realnz.com) or [0800 65 65 01](tel:08006565010). For
    transport enquiries within 24 hours of your departure, please contact Altitude Tours on
    [03 441 4788](tel:0344147880).
    [See here](https://www.realnz.com/en/terms-conditions/) for full Terms and Conditions.

    information about your Whanganui River canoe trip.
    Arrival & Accommodation
    ✅ Complimentary accommodation check-in is available from 4:00pm on the day prior to
    departure
    ✅ Late arrivals are welcome
    ✅ Accommodation operates as a self-service check-in system
    ✅ The sliding door on the carpark side of the building will remain unlocked for guest
    access
    ✅ Important trip information, room allocations, departure details, and barrel allocations
    will be displayed on the whiteboard in the lounge area
    ✅ Room keys will be left in the allocated room doors
    ✅ Waterproof storage barrels are located beside the lifejackets in the lounge area
    Before Departure
    ✅ All customers must complete and sign a waiver form prior to departure
    ✅ A full safety briefing and paddling instruction session will be provided before your
    journey
    ✅ Guests are encouraged to pack their waterproof barrels the evening prior to departure
    ✅ All barrels and equipment must be packed and placed outside on the deck area by 6:45am
    on departure morning
    Weather & River Conditions
    ⚠ River journeys are subject to weather, river levels, and safety conditions
    ⚠ Owhango Adventures may delay, postpone, or cancel departures if conditions are
    considered unsafe
    ⚠ If conditions improve, departures may be delayed or rescheduled to the following day
    ⚠ If Owhango Adventures cancels the trip and postponement is not possible, a full refund
    will be provided
    Freedom Hire Responsibility
    ⚠ This is a self-guided freedom hire journey
    ⚠ Customers are responsible for managing their own safety while on the river
    ⚠ If river conditions deteriorate during the journey, your first option should always be
    to wait for conditions to improve
    ⚠ If required due to weather or river conditions, customers may return a day later at no
    additional charge (subject to availability)
    Additional Costs
    ⚠ Any additional shuttle, recovery, or jet boat assistance required due to weather,
    fatigue, injury, or personal choice will be at the customer’s cost
    ⚠ Transfer to Pipiriki by jet boat is not included unless arranged separately
    Equipment & Liability
    ⚠ Customers are responsible for loss or damage to hired equipment
    ⚠ Owhango Adventures is not responsible for loss or damage to personal belongings,
    valuables, or electronics
    ⚠ All equipment is regularly inspected and maintained for safety and reliability
    Health & Safety
    ✅ A full safety briefing is provided before departure
    ✅ All paddlers must wear the provided life jacket / PFD at all times while on the river
    ✅ Alcohol and drugs are strictly prohibited during the journey
    ✅ Swimming ability is strongly recommended
    ✅ Moderate fitness is required as paddling can be physically demanding
    ✅ Customers with medical conditions, injuries, or disabilities that may affect safety
    must notify us before departure
    ✅ There is little to no cellphone reception across much of the journey
    Important Information
    ✅ Minimum age is 7 years
    ✅ School groups can request SOP / RAMS / safety documentation
    ✅ We strongly recommend arranging personal travel insurance
    ✅ Once payment has been made or the journey has started, refunds are not available for
    change of mind
    Thank you for choosing Owhango Adventures. We look forward to welcoming you on the
    Whanganui River.

    # Please read these notes carefully before your journey, as they contain important
    information about your guided Whanganui River experience.
    # Arrival & Accommodation
    ✅ Complimentary accommodation check-in is available from 4:00pm on the day prior to
    departure
    ✅ Late arrivals are welcome
    ✅ Accommodation operates as a self-service check-in system
    ✅ The sliding door on the carpark side of the building will remain unlocked for guest
    access
    ✅ Important trip information, room allocations, departure details, and guide information
    will be displayed on the whiteboard in the lounge area
    ✅ Room keys will be left in allocated room doors
    ✅ Free secure vehicle parking is available during your river journey
    # Before Departure
    ✅ A cooked breakfast is included on the morning of departure
    ✅ All customers must complete and sign a waiver form prior to departure
    ✅ A full safety briefing and paddling instruction session will be provided before the
    journey begins
    ✅ Your Kaitiaki guides will introduce the journey, river safety procedures, and cultural
    aspects of the Whanganui Awa
    ✅ Waterproof storage barrels and dry bags will be provided for personal gear
    # Departure Information
    ✅ Shuttle departure from Owhango is approximately 7:10am
    ✅ Customers will be transported to the Ohinepane river launch point
    ✅ Please ensure you are ready before departure time as the shuttle cannot be delayed
    # Your Guided River Journey
    ✅ This is a fully guided and fully catered cultural river experience
    ✅ Qualified Tangata Whenua Kaitiaki guides born and raised on the Whanganui Awa will
    accompany you throughout the journey
    ✅ Guests may choose to paddle in a 2-person canoe or travel in a traditional-style
    6-person Waka steered by your Kaitiaki
    ✅ Cultural storytelling, waiata, local history, and interpretation will be shared
    throughout the journey
    ✅ Overnight accommodation is at Maharanui Campsite within Whanganui National Park
    ✅ All camping gear and associated equipment can be provided if required
    # Meals & Dietary Requirements
    ✅ Fully catered meals, snacks, and drinks are included throughout the journey
    ✅ Dietary requirements can usually be accommodated
    ⚠ Additional charges may apply for specialised dietary requests
    # Journey Completion
    ✅ The journey concludes at Whakahoro on the second morning
    ✅ Pickup is approximately 9:30am at Whakahoro
    ✅ Return shuttle transport to Owhango is included
    ✅ Estimated arrival back to Owhango is approximately 10:30am – 11:00am
    # Weather & River Conditions
    ⚠ River journeys are subject to weather, river levels, and operational safety conditions
    ⚠ Owhango Adventures reserves the right to delay, postpone, modify, or cancel departures
    if conditions are considered unsafe
    ⚠ If conditions improve, departures may be delayed or rescheduled
    ⚠ If Owhango Adventures cancels the trip and postponement is not possible, a full refund
    will be provided
    # Health & Safety
    ✅ All participants must wear the provided lifejacket / PFD at all times while on the
    river
    ✅ Kaitiaki guides carry modern safety equipment including Garmin InReach emergency
    communication devices
    ✅ Swimming ability is strongly recommended
    ✅ Moderate fitness and mobility are required
    ✅ Alcohol and drugs are strictly prohibited during the journey
    ✅ Customers with medical conditions, injuries, allergies, or disabilities that may affect
    safety must notify us before departure
    ✅ There is limited to no cellphone reception across much of the river journey
    # Equipment & Liability
    ⚠ Owhango Adventures is not responsible for loss or damage to personal belongings,
    valuables, or electronics
    ⚠ Customers are encouraged to use additional waterproof protection for cameras and
    electronic devices
    ⚠ Outdoor adventure activities involve inherent risks including changing weather, river
    currents, and remote conditions
    # Important Information
    ✅ Minimum age is 7 years
    ✅ Children must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian
    ✅ Personal travel insurance is strongly recommended
    ✅ Refunds are not available for change of mind once payment has been made or the journey
    has commenced
    Thank you for choosing Owhango Adventures. We look forward to welcoming you onto the
    Whanganui Awa.

    **Please read the SAFETY INFORMATION below. 👇 It is important for your safety and
    enjoyment.**
    ##Sign your Waiver
    You as a participant must sign the waiver to be able to take part in this activity. So
    please click on the link above ☝️ and **Sign Digital Waiver** to complete your
    registration before your diving day.
    ##Meeting Point and Timing
    Please arrive at Gold Coast Dive Centre, 2/54-56 Paradise Ave Miami.
    Check-in times are the times shown on the booking (eg: for a 6:30 dive you need to be at
    the shop to check-in at 6:30). Please don't show up earlier for trips as we are unable to
    accommodate guests until the designated check-in times; there is adequate time after
    check-in to get everyone sorted.
    ##Parking
    We have Customer Parking Only, 2 hrs max at Gold Coast Dive Centre but there is free
    on-street parking on Paradise Ave. Currently, due to the ongoing roadworks in the area,
    parking can be limited on busy days so we do recommend allowing some extra time for
    parking.
    ##Scuba Diving in smooth waters
    Wave Break Island is located within the Gold Coast Broad-water (inshore) and is therefore
    protected from ocean swells. It provides an ideal environment for introductory diving or
    for someone who enjoys calm and easygoing conditions.
    ##First Time Scuba Diving
    Listen to your diving instructor above all else. No matter how experienced you might be,
    remember that your diving instructor is there to help you have a safe dive, first and
    foremost. If you're taking a scuba diving experience, then you should be certain to pay
    the utmost attention to what they are saying.
    ##Short notice plan updates may be sent
    Wave Break Island is tide-dependent, therefore departure times vary depending on tide
    times. Although we can predict the tide flow, in-water activity involves other conditions
    that are beyond our control. If trips are cancelled due to weather, please understand
    this is for safety reasons (yours and ours) and is outside of our control. We know
    cancellations can be frustrating but please understand that the weather and sea
    conditions can be unpredictable and changeable and, are outside of our control. Please be
    kind and polite to our staff who are only working towards a safe operation. We have a
    zero-tolerance policy for rudeness or aggression towards our customers and team.
    ##Boating
    Boating on the Gold Coast is as good as it gets anywhere on the planet, and Wave Break
    Island is a huge area of smooth water protected from ocean swell, therefore there are no
    waves and it is very rare to suffer from seasickness. Sea sickness is also known as
    travel sickness, if you have motion sickness it is recommended to take a seasickness
    remedy 30 minutes before boarding. Travacalm original, Travalcalm HO and Kwells are 3
    recommended types. Ginger/Natural remedy does not work.
    ##Wave Break Island's environmentally conscious behaviour
    In scuba diving, we often explore environments with biodiversity that is as exceptional
    as it is fragile. To limit our impact on the marine environment, there are a few simple
    rules we can all follow when snorkelling: no touching, collecting, damaging, feeding or
    moving marine life. Look and keep memories, but don’t touch and don’t chase or harass,
    please be mindful with your camera.
    ##Dive Etiquette
    - Respect Marine Life and Other Divers: No touch, No take.
    - Be mindful of your position in the water.
    - Take only photos, leave only bubbles.
    - If unsure of procedures, please ask Crew or staff.
    ##What to Bring
    Hat, sunscreen, snacks, water, camera, sunglasses, swimmers, towel, and anything you need
    for a day out in the sun and water. Otherwise, we are a Dive Centre and Retail Shop
    offering a wide variety of dive Gear to suit your needs and budget, there is a food
    machine in the shop.
    ##Personal Items
    Gold Coast Dive Centre and its employees take no responsibility for personal items or
    dive gear that are brought onto our property or used during activities whether lost,
    stolen or damaged. With any activity, there is a risk of damage to personal gear from
    handling or normal use. Personal items are brought onto the property and stored or used
    at the owners' own risk. After your activity, please double-check that you have
    everything with you before leaving. If personal items are not collected, they will be
    disposed of after three weeks.

    **Please read the SAFETY INFORMATION below. 👇 It is important for your safety and
    enjoyment.**
    ##Sign your Waiver
    You as a participant must sign the waiver to be able to take part in this activity. So
    please click on the link above ☝️ and **Sign Digital Waiver** to complete your
    registration before your snorkelling day.
    ##Meeting Point and Timing
    Please arrive at Gold Coast Dive Centre, 2/54-56 Paradise Ave Miami.
    Check-in times are the times shown on the booking (eg: for a 6:30 snorkel you need to be
    at the shop to check-in at 6:30). Please don't show up earlier for trips as we are unable
    to accommodate guests until the designated check-in times; there is adequate time after
    check-in to get everyone sorted.
    ##Parking
    We have Customer Parking Only, 2 hrs max at Gold Coast Dive Centre but there is free
    on-street parking on Paradise Ave. Currently, due to the ongoing roadworks in the area,
    parking can be limited on busy days so we do recommend allowing some extra time for
    parking.
    ##Snorkelling in smooth waters
    Wave Break Island is located within the Gold Coast Broad-water (inshore) and is therefore
    protected from ocean swells. It provides an ideal environment for beginners or for
    someone who enjoys calm and easygoing conditions.
    ##Experienced snorkellers
    Our snorkelling trips are primarily for surface snorkelling. We do not offer freediving
    or breath-hold diving and therefore snorkelling with a weight belt is not permitted.
    ##Short notice plan updates may be sent
    Wave Break Island is tide-dependent, therefore departure times vary depending on tide
    times. Although we can predict the tide flow, in-water activity involves other conditions
    that are beyond our control. If trips are cancelled due to weather, please understand
    this is for safety reasons (yours and ours) and is outside of our control. We know
    cancellations can be frustrating but please understand that the weather and sea
    conditions can be unpredictable and changeable and, are outside of our control. Please be
    kind and polite to our staff who are only working towards a safe operation. We have a
    zero-tolerance policy for rudeness or aggression towards our customers and team.
    ##Boating
    Boating on the Gold Coast is as good as it gets anywhere on the planet, and Wave Break
    Island is a huge area of smooth water protected from ocean swell, therefore there are no
    waves and it is very rare to suffer from seasickness. Sea sickness is also known as
    travel sickness, if you have motion sickness it is recommended to take a seasickness
    remedy 30 minutes before boarding. Travacalm original, Travalcalm HO and Kwells are 3
    recommended types. Ginger/Natural remedy does not work.
    ##Wave Break Island's environmentally conscious behaviour
    In snorkelling, we often explore environments with biodiversity that is as exceptional as
    it is fragile. To limit our impact on the marine environment, there are a few simple
    rules we can all follow when snorkelling: no touching, collecting, damaging, feeding or
    moving marine life. Look and keep memories, but don’t touch and don’t chase or harass,
    please be mindful with your camera.
    ##Snorkelling Etiquette
    - Check your gear prior to entering the water.
    - Stay close to your Guide or Buddy Up with a partner.
    - Know your limits, take it one step at a time.
    - Respect Marine Life and Other Snorkelers.
    - Keep your fins up, especially when swimming over shallower formations.
    ##Best Practices and Snorkel Briefing
    **Please read this safety information. It is important for your safety and enjoyment.**
    - All snorkelers are to be in “buddy pairs” to ensure the safety of each other. Children
    need to be under supervision at all times.
    - When snorkelling, the Boat must be visible at ALL TIMES. We need to see you to
    supervise you!
    - If the Boat Crew is signalling the OK signal, they are asking if you are OK. It
    requires an answer of “OK” or “Not OK” and “Help Me”.
    - Emergency recall to boat procedure (Continuous banging sound from boat or leader,
    continuous roaring Boat Engine).
    - Exit: remove fins before boarding, please leave your mask on. Hold on to the boat while
    taking your fins off.
    - Avoid the area around Engines, if they are running, do not come close without
    instruction from the Boat Crew.
    - Protect the Marine Park: No touch, No take.
    - If unsure of procedures, please ask Crew or staff.
    ##What to Bring
    Hat, sunscreen, snacks, water, camera, sunglasses, swimmers, towel, and anything you need
    for a day out in the sun and water. Otherwise, we are a Dive Centre and Retail Shop
    offering a wide variety of snorkel Gear to suit your needs and budget, there is a food
    machine in the shop.
    ##Personal Items
    Gold Coast Dive Centre and its employees take no responsibility for personal items or
    dive gear that are brought onto our property or used during activities whether lost,
    stolen or damaged. With any activity, there is a risk of damage to personal gear from
    handling or normal use. Personal items are brought onto the property and stored or used
    at the owners' own risk. After your activity, please double-check that you have
    everything with you before leaving. If personal items are not collected, they will be
    disposed of after three weeks.

================================================================================================
  stratum   : heading_rich   words 1033   headings 27

    #🏝️ Cook Island Trip – Confirmation & Safety Info
    We’re excited to have you joining us for a trip at Cook Island (Jungarra Ngarrian) — one
    of Australia’s top marine reserves!
    ###Please read the key info below to ensure a smooth and safe day.
    ---
    **1. Sign Your Waiver**
    All participant must complete the digital waiver before arrival.
    You'll find the link in your booking confirmation email.
    Please complete it in advance to avoid delays at check-in.
    ---
    **2. Meeting Point & Timing**
    Gold Coast Dive Centre
    2/54–56 Paradise Ave, Miami QLD
    Please arrive at the time shown on your booking
    (e.g., for a 6:30 trip, check in by 6:30).
    We can’t accommodate early arrivals, but there will be plenty of time to get ready once
    checked in.
    ---
    **3. Parking**
    Free on-street parking nearby.
    Please allow extra time for parking, especially during busy periods or roadworks
    ---
    **4. Swimming Ability, Confidence & Fitness**
    Cook Island is an open-ocean site. Conditions can vary and may include currents, swells,
    and winds.
    Snorkelers should be confident, fit and competent to swim in open-water conditions.
    If you have not snorkeling experience or haven't snorkeled in the past 12-24 months, we
    strongly recommend booking extra supervision or a private guide.
    ---
    **5. Surface Snorkeling Only**
    Our snorkel trips are for surface snorkelling only.
    We do not offer freediving or breath-hold diving.
    Weight belts are not permitted.
    ---
    **6. Weather & Plan Changes**
    Cook Island is weather-dependent, and sometimes trips get cancelled due to conditions.
    Weather is unpredictable and cancellations are beyond our control.
    We appreciate your patience and understanding as we prioritise safety.
    ---
    **7. Seasickness & Remedies**
    Due to the location of Cook Island, seasickness can be an issue.
    We recommend taking a seasickness remedy (e.g., Travacalm, Travalcalm HO, or Kwells) 30
    minutes before boarding.
    Bring extra remedies with you — Natural remedies (like ginger) are not as effective.
    ---
    **8. What to Bring**
    Pack light — space on the boat is limited!
    Only bring the essentials:
    - swimmer
    - towel,
    - sunscreen
    - water
    - light snack
    Avoid large bags or bulky items.
    ---
    **9. Gear Handling**
    You’ll carry your snorkel gear from the trailer to the boat (approx. 50m).
    Please handle all equipment with care.
    After the trip:
    - Return all gear to the trailer at the jetty
    - Once back at the dive centre, rinse the gear you used in the designated wash area
    - Turn wetsuits right-side out before placing them in the rinse station
    Thanks for helping us look after shared gear.
    ---
    **10. Boating Etiquette**
    - Always wear your life jacket when instructed
    - Stay seated when the boat is in motion
    - Maintain three points of contact when walking on the boat
    - Stay clear of running engines
    - Pay attention to the safety briefings
    - Respect everyone’s space
    - Keep personal items tidy and out of the way
    - Never throw anything overboard
    ---
    **11. Buddy System**
    - All snorkelers must remain in buddy pairs at all times
    - Children must remain under direct supervision
    - The boat must remain visible at all times
    If unsure at any time — signal the crew immediately.
    ---
    **12. Hand Signals (Always Required Response)**
    All snorkelers will be briefed on signals before entering the water.
    **Hand Signals (Always Required Response)**
    When crew signal you, you must respond:
    - OK → Make a clear “OK” sign with your hand above the water.
    - Not OK → Raise one arm straight up above your head
    - Help / Distress → Wave one arm side to side above your head until assisted
    ---
    **Whistle Signals**
    1 Whistle Blast
    Attention / Routine Communication
    → Stop and look toward the boat
    → Respond with OK or Not OK
    2 Whistle Blasts
    Assistance Required / Prepare for Pickup
    → Stay with your buddy
    → Calmly begin making your way toward the boat
    3 Whistle Blasts (Repeated)
    Emergency – Immediate Response Required
    → Return to the boat immediately
    → Raise one arm if assistance is needed
    ---
    **Emergency Recall (Boat Signal)**
    If you hear:
    - Continuous loud banging on the hull
    - Repeated engine revving
    This means full recall to the boat immediately.
    Stop what you are doing, stay with your buddy, and return directly to the vessel.
    ---
    **Exit Procedure**
    - Approach the boat calmly and wait for crew instruction
    - Keep your mask on and snorkel in place while approaching the boat
    - Remove your fins in the water while holding the ladder
    - Hand fins to crew if instructed
    - Board carefully using three points of contact
    Once onboard:
    - Keep your mask either on your face or secured around your neck — do not carry it
    loosely
    - Store fins neatly in the designated area
    - Do not leave fins, masks, snorkels, or weight belts in walkways or seating areas
    - Keep the deck clear at all times to avoid trip hazards
    ---
    **13. Personal Items**
    Gold Coast Dive Centre isn’t responsible for personal items.
    Any gear or items brought on the trip are at your own risk. We are not liable for loss,
    theft, or damage.
    Please check your belongings before leaving. Unclaimed items will be disposed of after a
    week.
    We do not provide storage.
    ---
    #🐢Cook Island Marine Reserve Code of Conduct
    ###Cook Island is a protected aquatic reserve. Help us protect it.
    ---
    - Look, don’t touch marine life, even shells
    - Keep your distance — Don’t chase or crowd animals
    - Stay 3+ metres from turtles and never block their path
    - No feeding or baiting marine life
    - Don’t rest or grab rocks or reef
    - Control your fins to avoid contact with reef or sediment
    - Maintain buoyancy and stay horizontal above the seabed
    - Secure all gear to prevent dragging
    - Avoid flash or prolonged light when photographing
    - Use reef-safe sunscreen or wear protection
    - Leave artefacts undisturbed
    - Remove floating litter if safe to do so
    ---
    **By completing your booking, you acknowledge that you’ve read and understood the safety
    guidelines and requirements outlined above.**
    Thank you for diving responsibly and helping us protect this special marine environment.
    **Gold Coast Dive Centre Team**
    ---

    [health_safety] *NEW*
        Due to the location of Cook Island, seasickness can be an issue.
        We recommend taking a seasickness remedy (e.g., Travacalm, Travalcalm HO, or Kwells)
        30 minutes before boarding.
        Bring extra remedies with you — Natural remedies (like ginger) are not as effective.
        Hand Signals (Always Required Response):
        All snorkelers will be briefed on signals before entering the water.
        When crew signal you, you must respond:
        OK → Make a clear “OK” sign with your hand above the water.
        Not OK → Raise one arm straight up above your head
        Help / Distress → Wave one arm side to side above your head until assisted
        Whistle Signals:
        1 Whistle Blast: Attention / Routine Communication
        Stop and look toward the boat
        Respond with OK or Not OK
        2 Whistle Blasts: Assistance Required / Prepare for Pickup
        Stay with your buddy
        Calmly begin making your way toward the boat
        3 Whistle Blasts (Repeated): Emergency – Immediate Response Required
        Return to the boat immediately
        Raise one arm if assistance is needed
        Emergency Recall (Boat Signal):
        If you hear:
        Continuous loud banging on the hull
        Repeated engine revving
        This means full recall to the boat immediately.
        Stop what you are doing, stay with your buddy, and return directly to the vessel.
        Exit Procedure:
        Approach the boat calmly and wait for crew instruction
        Keep your mask on and snorkel in place while approaching the boat
        Remove your fins in the water while holding the ladder
        Hand fins to crew if instructed
        Board carefully using three points of contact
        Once onboard:
        Keep your mask either on your face or secured around your neck — do not carry it
        loosely
        Store fins neatly in the designated area
        Do not leave fins, masks, snorkels, or weight belts in walkways or seating areas
        Keep the deck clear at all times to avoid trip hazards

    ##Check in closes 15 minutes prior to departure. Gate closes 5 minutes prior to departure
    time
    ##What to bring
    • Non-slip shoes/boots
    • Waterproof jacket
    • Warm sweater/fleece jacket
    • Sunscreen/ sunglasses
    • Insect repellent
    • Camera/phone
    • Personal medication, including for asthma and allergies
    Cabinet café food and snacks will be available for purchase onboard. The Haven is
    cashless, so please come prepared.
    ##Milford Sound Risk Disclosure
    Visitors to Milford Sound should be aware of various natural hazards when going to
    Milford Sound.
    **Aotearoa New Zealand**
    - Powerful natural forces have shaped Aotearoa New Zealand over millions of years.
    Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of the Pacific Ocean. They
    have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.
    - Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each
    year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage. Understanding
    the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your visit.
    **Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one of the world’s most
    spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep fiord
    have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
    - The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any
    time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes,
    landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    - It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a short
    stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it becomes.
    Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you understand
    the risks, before you go.
    **Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland.
    We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a normal part of
    how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
    Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They
    might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or
    disrupt your visit.
    - Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides.
    These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your
    travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
    - Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But
    they will happen again.
    - The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the
    entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or
    greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this happening in
    the next 50 years (find out more at [af8.org.nz)](https://af8.org.nz/). An earthquake of
    this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.
    **What to do in an earthquake:**
    - DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when
    you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less
    likely you are to be injured.
    - Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers)
    as quickly as possible.
    **Landslides at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - steep mountains around Piopiotahi Milford Sound are prone to rockfall and landslides.
    Earthquakes and severe weather can make the cliffs unstable, sending rock and debris down
    at speed.
    - Smaller rockfalls are common but often go unnoticed, unless you are nearby.
    - Bigger landslides do not happen often. The chance of one occurring during a short visit
    is extremely unlikely. However, they could cause a tsunami in the fiord and do pose a
    risk to life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    - Large earthquakes are the most common trigger of big landslides in Fiordland. A large
    earthquake during your visit is extremely unlikely, especially for a short stay.
    **Be prepared for landslides**
    - Take extra supplies, food, water, first aid, clothes in your vehicle when travelling in
    remote areas, in case you get stuck – The road from Te Anau to Piopiotahi Milford Sound,
    is prone to avalanches, rockfall and landslides. It is monitored 24/7 by the Milford Road
    Alliance. However, if you get stuck, it will take time for help to reach you. Having
    extra supplies in your vehicle will make the wait time more comfortable.
    - If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust clouds, loud rumbling, or
    splashing. Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord
    and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    **Tsunami at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Like all of Aotearoa New Zealand’s coastline, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is at risk of
    tsunami from multiple sources.
    - The most common threat comes from distant earthquakes in the Pacific Ocean. These
    ocean-source tsunamis take hours to reach our shores. Official warnings are issued in
    time for people to move to safety.
    - Less common, but of more concern, is the potential for a large landslide to fall into
    the fiord and trigger a tsunami.
    - Landslide-triggered tsunamis are rare. The chance of one occurring during your visit is
    extremely unlikely. However, they can create large waves and do pose a risk to life at
    Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    **Be prepared for tsunamis**
    - Triggered by an earthquake – If you feel a LONG (1 minute or more) or STRONG (cannot
    stand up) earthquake, while at Piopiotahi Milford Sound, Get GONE. Move up and away from
    waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    - Triggered by a landslide – If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust
    clouds, loud rumbling, splashing or unusual water behavior, GET GONE. Move up and away
    from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    **Plans and preparedness**
    - Piopiotahi Milford Sound has emergency response plans. These coordinate multiple
    agencies in a State or Emergency. The plans cover earthquakes, tsunami, landslides,
    avalanches, flooding, severe weather and other emergencies.
    - All tourism operators maintain their own emergency procedures. These integrate with the
    wider response in a State of Emergency.
    - If a large landslide triggers a tsunami, there will be no warning. Emergency support
    will take time to arrive. Visitors and workers should be aware of the risk to life and
    prepared to move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as
    possible.
    For more detailed information, please visit [Emergency Management
    Southland](https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or
    [AF8](https://af8.org.nz/).

    avalanches, flooding, severe weather and other emergencies.
    - All tourism operators maintain their own emergency procedures. These integrate with the
    wider response in a State of Emergency.
    - If a large landslide triggers a tsunami, there will be no warning. Emergency support
    will take time to arrive. Visitors and workers should be aware of the risk to life and
    prepared to move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as
    possible.
    For more detailed information, please visit [Emergency Management
    Southland](https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or
    [AF8](https://af8.org.nz/).

    [health_safety] *NEW*
        Milford Sound Risk Disclosure:
        Visitors to Milford Sound should be aware of various natural hazards when going to
        Milford Sound.
        Aotearoa New Zealand:
        Powerful natural forces have shaped Aotearoa New Zealand over millions of years.
        Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of the Pacific Ocean.
        They have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.
        Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each
        year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage.
        Understanding the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your
        visit.
        Piopiotahi Milford Sound:
        Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one of the world’s most
        spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep
        fiord have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
        The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any
        time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes,
        landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
        It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a
        short stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it
        becomes. Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you
        understand the risks, before you go.
        Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound:
        Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in
        Fiordland. We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a
        normal part of how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
        Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
        They might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major
        impacts or disrupt your visit.
        Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides.
        These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your
        travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
        Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit.
        But they will happen again.
        The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the
        entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or
        greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this
        happening in the next 50 years (find out more at af8.org.nz) (https://af8.org.nz/).
        An earthquake of this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and
        surrounding area.
        What to do in an earthquake:
        DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when
        you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less
        likely you are to be injured.
        Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and
        rivers) as quickly as possible.
        Landslides at Piopiotahi Milford Sound:
        steep mountains around Piopiotahi Milford Sound are prone to rockfall and landslides.
        Earthquakes and severe weather can make the cliffs unstable, sending rock and debris
        down at speed.
        Smaller rockfalls are common but often go unnoticed, unless you are nearby.
        Bigger landslides do not happen often. The chance of one occurring during a short
        visit is extremely unlikely. However, they could cause a tsunami in the fiord and do
        pose a risk to life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
        Large earthquakes are the most common trigger of big landslides in Fiordland. A large
        earthquake during your visit is extremely unlikely, especially for a short stay.
        Be prepared for landslides:
        Take extra supplies, food, water, first aid, clothes in your vehicle when travelling
        in remote areas, in case you get stuck – The road from Te Anau to Piopiotahi Milford
        Sound, is prone to avalanches, rockfall and landslides. It is monitored 24/7 by the
        Milford Road Alliance. However, if you get stuck, it will take time for help to reach
        you. Having extra supplies in your vehicle will make the wait time more comfortable.
        If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust clouds, loud rumbling, or
        splashing. Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the
        fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
        Tsunami at Piopiotahi Milford Sound:
        Like all of Aotearoa New Zealand’s coastline, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is at risk of
        tsunami from multiple sources.
        The most common threat comes from distant earthquakes in the Pacific Ocean. These
        ocean-source tsunamis take hours to reach our shores. Official warnings are issued in
        time for people to move to safety.
        Less common, but of more concern, is the potential for a large landslide to fall into
        the fiord and trigger a tsunami.
        Landslide-triggered tsunamis are rare. The chance of one occurring during your visit
        is extremely unlikely. However, they can create large waves and do pose a risk to
        life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
        Be prepared for tsunamis:
        Triggered by an earthquake – If you feel a LONG (1 minute or more) or STRONG (cannot
        stand up) earthquake, while at Piopiotahi Milford Sound, Get GONE. Move up and away
        from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
        Triggered by a landslide – If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust
        clouds, loud rumbling, splashing or unusual water behavior, GET GONE. Move up and
        away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
        Plans and preparedness:
        Piopiotahi Milford Sound has emergency response plans. These coordinate multiple
        agencies in a State or Emergency. The plans cover earthquakes, tsunami, landslides,
        avalanches, flooding, severe weather and other emergencies.
        All tourism operators maintain their own emergency procedures. These integrate with
        the wider response in a State of Emergency.
        If a large landslide triggers a tsunami, there will be no warning. Emergency support
        will take time to arrive. Visitors and workers should be aware of the risk to life
        and prepared to move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as
        possible.
        For more detailed information, please visit Emergency Management Southland
        (https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or AF8
        (https://af8.org.nz/).

    ##Important Information
    #Boarding Time: 30 Minutes Prior to Schedule Cruise Time!!
    **Location**: Aqua Adventure Centre, 95 Marine Parade, Southport 4215
    **Meeting Point**: Once you arrive at the Aqua Adventures Centre, please meet the Spirit
    Team outside of the Broadwater Cafe. Our meeting location is on the grass, on the
    left-hand-side of the Broadwater Cafe.
    **Map**: Please see attached.
    **Departure Location**
    [Aqua Adventure Centre, 95 Marine Parade, Southport 4215.
    ](https://maps.app.goo.gl/iV6RH53DJCDtHuUT9)
    **What to Bring:**
    Pack a warm jumper and a windproof/waterproof jacket as conditions at sea can be windier
    and cooler than in the marina.
    Life is bright, you gotta have shades!
    You may bring a camera, mobile phone, etc. However, since you may be splashed with ocean
    spray, please bring these items at your own risk.
    **Sea Sickness**
    For your comfort and to ensure you have an enjoyable whale watching experience, if you
    have not travelled on the open ocean before or suffer from any sort of travel sickness,
    we highly recommend taking sea sickness medication prior to boarding the cruise.
    ![Description of image](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/8ahnuiwlQJONlHofdYlK)
    #How to Get Here
    **Driving from North/Brisbane:**
    * Take the Pacific Motorway (M1) southbound and exit at Smith Street Motorway.
    * Follow signs to Southport and continue to Marine Parade.
    * Parking is available nearby along Marine Parade and surrounding streets.
    **Driving from South/NSW:**
    * Head north on the M1 towards Gold Coast.
    * Exit onto Gold Coast Highway towards Southport.
    * Turn onto Marine Parade and continue to number 95.
    * Parking is available along Marine Parade and nearby side streets.
    **Public transport from Brisbane/North:**
    * Take the Gold Coast Train to Helensvale Station.
    * Transfer to the G:link light rail towards Broadbeach.
    * Disembark at Southport Station.
    * It’s a short walk (approx. 8 minutes) down to 95 Marine Parade.
    **Public transport from Surfers Paradise/South:**
    * Take the G:link light rail towards Helensvale.
    * Disembark at Southport Station.
    * Walk approx. 8 minutes down to 95 Marine Parade.

    ✔ Lounge area

    ✔ Charging facilities
    This provides a convenient place to rest, recharge devices, reorganize gear, and prepare
    for the next section of the trail.

        When passing through Owhango during your Te Araroa walk, hikers are welcome to camp
        free of charge at our Owhango base.
        Facilities available include:
        Showers
        Toilets
        Free WiFi
        Lounge area
        BBQ facilities
        Microwave
        Jug and toaster
        Charging facilities
        This provides a convenient place to rest, recharge devices, reorganize gear, and
        prepare for the next section of the trail.
        Two River Departure Options:
        Option 1 – Continue Walking to Whakahoro:
        Continue hiking from National Park / Waimarino to Whakahoro over the following days.
        We will meet you at Whakahoro with:
        Your groceries
        Canoe
        Paddling equipment
        Dry barrels
        River maps
        At Whakahoro we will:
        Conduct a full safety briefing
        Assist with packing dry barrels
        Explain river logistics and safety procedures
        Provide river maps and tide information
        You will then begin your self-guided Whanganui River Journey.
        Option 2 – Shuttle Back to Owhango:
        If preferred, we can collect hikers from National Park / Waimarino and return you to
        our Owhango base.
        You may then:
        Camp free of charge at our base
        Reorganize equipment
        Prepare for the river section
        The following morning, you will travel with us to Whakahoro to begin the river
        journey.

    tours at any time as required.

    passengers and 2 crew members in 1C class waters.

    Epic Marine Charters - Busselton Cruises.
    Activities include but are not limited to, access to jetties, wharves, or access areas,
    embarking and disembarking of vessel, entering and exiting the water, whilst on vessel,
    in water activities, affiliates or venues.
    It is the sole responsibility of passengers to ensure their own safety, behaviour and

    This includes following all directions given by staff.

    any time, who or by way of deliberate act, wilful damage, is deemed or behaves in a

    ##Your Trail Riding Party Plan
    Upon arrival at Darkes Forest Riding Ranch the Birthday girl/boy will be greeted by
    his/her party host who will be in charge of making sure the celebration is unforgettable.
    Before the party commences it is important, we have all necessary paper work in order and
    each child is fitted with a safety helmet, your party host will take you over to the
    office to complete. Please ensure all riders come wearing enclosed shoes. The host will
    then introduce herself to the group and outline the order of events before heading over
    to the trail ride manager to pair each guest up with their horses.
    A safety demonstration will now take place to ensure all riders are confident,
    comfortable and ready to head out into the native bushland to enjoy the fun and adventure
    that horse riding at Darkes Forest has to offers. Your party host as well as other
    experienced instructors will take care of the group while out on trail ☺☺ The number of
    instructors is determined by the size
    and experience of the group.
    Any parents or siblings that are not heading out on trail are welcome to enjoy the
    facilities of the Lazy Haze Kiosk on site, or have a walk around the property. For safety
    reasons please do not approach the horses at any time without permission or assistance
    from staff.
    Once the riders return from trail they will dismount and head over to the public area
    with the advice of instructors. After securing the horses the instructor will re gather
    the group and horse grooming and basic horsemanship will commence followed by a party
    game (time permitting)
    We do provide lunch in the form of hot party style food along with fairy bread etc. Food
    may vary slightly from party to party at our discretion. If you do not wish for us to
    provide food your party cost will be adjusted accordingly. Please be sure to note this
    and any dietary requirements on your booking sheet. Once everyone has eaten, we will
    commence birthday formalities of singing happy birthday and cutting the cake. This is a
    great time for photo opportunities.
    After Cake we will conclude your Party by presenting the birthday girl/boy with a special
    gift from us and thanking the group for spending the day with us at Darkes Forest Riding
    Ranch.
    The cost of you Trail Ride Party for up to 6 riders including the Birthday girl/boy is
    $850-for a half hour trail ride and $950-for a 1hour trail ride. The party duration is
    1.5-2hours accordingly. Of course, you can have more than six riders they are just
    charged at $100.00 per head thereafter. The maximum party size for trail ride parties is
    10 guests. Please bring along the cake and any lolly bags or gifts you wish to hand out
    and we will take care of the rest.
    We look forward to a day of happy trails making birthday memories to last a lifetime ☺☺

    ##Your Pony Party Plan
    Upon arrival at Darkes Forest Riding Ranch the Birthday girl/boy will be greeted by
    his/her party host who will be in charge of making sure the celebration is unforgettable.
    Before the party commences it is important, we have a ll necessary paper work in order
    and each child is fitted with a safety helmet, your party host will take you over to the
    office to complete.
    The host will then introduce herself to the group and outline the order of events before
    gathering the ponies an d heading off to the assigned pony ride area.
    A safety demonstration will now take place to ensure all riders are confident,
    comfortable and ready to get the most out of the pony ride experience. Please ensure all
    guests are wearing enclosed shoes.
    Each child will take turns of riding the ponies under the care of the party host and pony
    leaders. The time each child spends on the pony is determined by the number of guests in
    the group and will be worked out by the party host. If time permits each child wil l have
    the opportunity to have two pony rides each. ☺ ☺
    Once the entire group have finished their pony rides the host will secure the ponies and
    commence grooming and basic horsemanship hints and tips. The children will have the
    opportunity to pat the pony and tell it a secret. A party game will now be played. The
    amount of time spent on games is time permitting and at the discretion of the party host.
    With the direction of the instructors the group will then head back down to the reception
    area for lunch. We do provide lunch in the form of hot party style food along with fairy
    bread etc. Food may vary slightly from party to party at our discretion. Please be sure
    to note any dietary requirements on your booking sheet. Once everyone has eaten, we will
    commence birthday formalities of singing happy birthday and cutting the cake. This is a
    great time for photo opportunities. After Cake we will conclude your Party by presenting
    the birthday girl/boy with a special gift from us and thanking the group for spending the
    day with us at Darkes Forest Riding Ranch.
    For up to 8 guests, of course you can have more, they are just charged at a small fee of
    $55 per head. If you have less than a group of 8 that is also fine. The cost does not
    change however your guests can expect more one on one time with the ponies. Party
    duration is minimum 1.5k 2hrs depending on the number of guests attending.
    Please bring along your cake as well as any lolly bags or gifts you wish to hand out, we
    will take care of the rest. If you do not wish for us to provide food that is also fine
    and your cost will be adjusted accordingly.
    We look forward to partying Pony style with you ☺ ☺

    ##Includes return journey back to Queenstown
    ##What to bring
    • Non-slip shoes/boots
    • Waterproof jacket
    • Warm sweater/fleece jacket
    • Sunscreen/sunglasses
    • Insect repellent
    • Camera/phone
    • Personal medication, including for asthma and allergies
    This is a cashless experience so please come prepared.
    ##Milford Sound Risk Disclosure
    Visitors to Milford Sound should be aware of various natural hazards when going to
    Milford Sound.
    **Aotearoa New Zealand**
    - Powerful natural forces have shaped Aotearoa New Zealand over millions of years.
    Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of the Pacific Ocean. They
    have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.
    - Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each
    year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage. Understanding
    the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your visit.
    **Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one of the world’s most
    spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep fiord
    have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
    - The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any
    time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes,
    landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    - It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a short
    stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it becomes.
    Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you understand
    the risks, before you go.
    **Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland.
    We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a normal part of
    how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
    Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They
    might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or
    disrupt your visit.
    - Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides.
    These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your
    travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
    - Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But
    they will happen again.
    - The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the
    entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or
    greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this happening in
    the next 50 years (find out more at [af8.org.nz)](https://af8.org.nz/). An earthquake of
    this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.
    **What to do in an earthquake:**
    - DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when
    you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less
    likely you are to be injured.
    - Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers)
    as quickly as possible.
    **Landslides at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - steep mountains around Piopiotahi Milford Sound are prone to rockfall and landslides.
    Earthquakes and severe weather can make the cliffs unstable, sending rock and debris down
    at speed.
    - Smaller rockfalls are common but often go unnoticed, unless you are nearby.
    - Bigger landslides do not happen often. The chance of one occurring during a short visit
    is extremely unlikely. However, they could cause a tsunami in the fiord and do pose a
    risk to life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    - Large earthquakes are the most common trigger of big landslides in Fiordland. A large
    earthquake during your visit is extremely unlikely, especially for a short stay.
    **Be prepared for landslides**
    - Take extra supplies, food, water, first aid, clothes in your vehicle when travelling in
    remote areas, in case you get stuck – The road from Te Anau to Piopiotahi Milford Sound,
    is prone to avalanches, rockfall and landslides. It is monitored 24/7 by the Milford Road
    Alliance. However, if you get stuck, it will take time for help to reach you. Having
    extra supplies in your vehicle will make the wait time more comfortable.
    - If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust clouds, loud rumbling, or
    splashing. Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord
    and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    **Tsunami at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Like all of Aotearoa New Zealand’s coastline, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is at risk of
    tsunami from multiple sources.
    - The most common threat comes from distant earthquakes in the Pacific Ocean. These
    ocean-source tsunamis take hours to reach our shores. Official warnings are issued in
    time for people to move to safety.
    - Less common, but of more concern, is the potential for a large landslide to fall into
    the fiord and trigger a tsunami.
    - Landslide-triggered tsunamis are rare. The chance of one occurring during your visit is
    extremely unlikely. However, they can create large waves and do pose a risk to life at
    Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    **Be prepared for tsunamis**
    - Triggered by an earthquake – If you feel a LONG (1 minute or more) or STRONG (cannot
    stand up) earthquake, while at Piopiotahi Milford Sound, Get GONE. Move up and away from
    waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    - Triggered by a landslide – If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust
    clouds, loud rumbling, splashing or unusual water behavior, GET GONE. Move up and away
    from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    **Plans and preparedness**
    - Piopiotahi Milford Sound has emergency response plans. These coordinate multiple
    agencies in a State or Emergency. The plans cover earthquakes, tsunami, landslides,
    avalanches, flooding, severe weather and other emergencies.
    - All tourism operators maintain their own emergency procedures. These integrate with the
    wider response in a State of Emergency.
    - If a large landslide triggers a tsunami, there will be no warning. Emergency support
    will take time to arrive. Visitors and workers should be aware of the risk to life and
    prepared to move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as
    possible.
    For more detailed information, please visit [Emergency Management
    Southland](https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or
    [AF8](https://af8.org.nz/).
    **Contact Us**
    For enquiries about your reservation, please contact the RealNZ team on
    [contact@realnz.com](mailto:contact@realnz.com) or [0800 65 65 01](tel:08006565010). For
    transport enquiries within 24 hours of your departure, please contact Altitude Tours on
    [03 441 4788](tel:0344147880).
    [See here](https://www.realnz.com/en/terms-conditions/) for full Terms and Conditions.

    ## Thank You for Booking with Canyoning New Zealand!
    We're excited to welcome you on our **Glenorchy Paradise Full Day Adventure** and can't
    wait to share one of New Zealand’s most spectacular wilderness experiences with you.
    ## Before Your Adventure
    ### Meeting Locations & Parking
    Please check your booking carefully and arrive at the meeting location selected for your
    tour.
    **Queenstown Pick-Up – 08:45am meeting time**
    Please wait outside the Eichardt’s Hotel.
    **Address:** 2 Marine Parade, Queenstown 9300
    [Google Maps Pin](https://maps.app.goo.gl/pK9XELRkRrU83L1Z8)
    **Glenorchy Pick-Up – 09:45am meeting time**
    Please wait outside the Mrs Woolly's General Store.
    **Address:** 64 Oban Street, Glenorchy, 9372
    [Google Maps Pin](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Gg5fQHPvYDYL3VBw5)
    Please note that parking is not available at our Queenstown or Glenorchy pick-up
    locations. If you are driving, please allow extra time to find parking nearby and walk to
    the meeting point before your scheduled check-in time.
    Central Queenstown Parking Suggestion
    **Address:** 10 Boundary Street, Queenstown 9300
    [Google Maps Pin](https://maps.app.goo.gl/wCbBz8Pn6U2zLY1i9)
    Central Glenorchy Parking Suggestion
    **Address:** Glenorchy Waterfront Reserve Road, Glenorchy 9372
    [Google Maps Pin](https://maps.app.goo.gl/8k8vcvaHdeSs1rG97)
    ### Important: Please Arrive on Time
    Our guides begin preparing the group as soon as check-in opens to ensure a safe and
    timely departure. As we operate multiple tours each day and need to respect the schedules
    of all guests, we are unable to delay departures for late arrivals.
    ### What to Bring
    Please bring:
    * Swimwear to wear under your wetsuit
    * A towel for after the adventure
    * A personal water bottle
    * Any personal medications you may require
    For your peace of mind, we recommend leaving unnecessary valuables at home.
    Your dry clothes and personal belongings can be stored in our locked vehicle while you
    are in the canyon. While we have never experienced any security issues, we still
    recommend bringing only what you need for the adventure.
    ### Lunch is included
    A fresh picnic-style lunch is included and will be provided during the day.
    ### Important Safety Information
    Please take the time to review our risk acknowledgement Information before your
    adventure:
    **[Please Read](https://www.canyoningnewzealand.co.nz/safety/)**
    Please contact us before your tour if you have any injuries, medical conditions, or
    concerns about your suitability for the activity. Please also note that all bookings are
    subject to our 48-hour cancellation policy.
    ### Need Assistance?
    Our friendly reservations team is here to help.
    **Phone:** +64 3 428 0071
    **Open daily:** 8:00am – 8:00pm
    ### Tiaki Promise
    New Zealand is a truly special place, and everyone who lives here or visits has a
    responsibility to help protect it. The Tiaki Promise is a commitment to care for
    Aotearoa, now and for future generations.
    By embracing the Tiaki Promise, you are choosing to act as a guardian — respecting the
    land, protecting the environment, and preserving the natural beauty we are privileged to
    explore.
    **Nau mai, haere mai ki Aotearoa — Welcome to New Zealand!**
    **[Learn more](https://www.tiakinewzealand.com/en_NZ/)**
    ### Help Keep New Zealand Wild
    We're committed to reducing our environmental impact and offsetting our carbon footprint
    by planting native trees throughout the Wakatipu region.
    If you'd like to support this initiative, you can make a voluntary $5 contribution here:
    **[Donate
    Now](https://fareharbor.com/embeds/book/canyoningnewzealand/items/387858/calendar/?flow=489300&full-items=yes)**
    Thank you for choosing Canyoning New Zealand. We look forward to sharing an unforgettable
    day of adventure, wilderness and incredible scenery with you.
    See you soon!

    recommend bringing only what you need for the adventure.
    ### Important Safety Information
    Please take the time to review our risk acknowledgement Information before your
    adventure:
    **[Please Read](https://www.canyoningnewzealand.co.nz/safety/)**
    Please contact us before your tour if you have any injuries, medical conditions, or
    concerns about your suitability for the activity. Please also note that all bookings are
    subject to our 48-hour cancellation policy.
    ### Need Assistance?
    Our friendly reservations team is here to help.
    **Phone:** +64 3 428 0071
    **Open daily:** 8:00am – 8:00pm
    ### Tiaki Promise
    New Zealand is a truly special place, and everyone who lives here or visits has a
    responsibility to help protect it. The Tiaki Promise is a commitment to care for
    Aotearoa, now and for future generations.
    By embracing the Tiaki Promise, you are choosing to act as a guardian — respecting the
    land, protecting the environment, and preserving the natural beauty we are privileged to
    explore.
    **Nau mai, haere mai ki Aotearoa — Welcome to New Zealand!**
    **[Learn more](https://www.tiakinewzealand.com/en_NZ/)**

    day of adventure, wilderness and incredible scenery with you.

    ##Milford Sound Signature Cruise
    Please collect your boarding passes at least 20 minutes prior to departure time by
    checking in with one of the RealNZ team at the Milford Sound Visitor Terminal.
    **Parking at Milford Sound**
    The car park closest to the Milford Sound Visitor Terminal is about a 5–10 minute walk
    and costs $10 per hour. There is free parking on Deepwater Basin Road, about a 20-minute
    scenic walk to the terminal. Please allow 45 minutes to an hour for parking and check-in
    before your cruise.
    Be sure to stay informed about road conditions by checking the NZTA website
    [here](https://www.nzta.govt.nz/projects/sh94-milford-road/). In the winter months,
    remember to carry snow chains and be ready for possible delays.
    **What to bring**
    • Non-slip shoes/boots
    • Waterproof jacket
    • Warm sweater/fleece jacket
    • Sunscreen/ sunglasses
    • Insect repellent
    • Camera/phone
    • Personal medication, including for asthma and allergies
    ##Milford Sound Risk Disclosure
    Visitors to Milford Sound should be aware of various natural hazards when going to
    Milford Sound.
    **Aotearoa New Zealand**
    - Powerful natural forces have shaped Aotearoa New Zealand over millions of years.
    Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of the Pacific Ocean. They
    have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.
    - Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each
    year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage. Understanding
    the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your visit.
    **Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one of the world’s most
    spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep fiord
    have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
    - The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any
    time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes,
    landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    - It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a short
    stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it becomes.
    Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you understand
    the risks, before you go.
    **Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland.
    We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a normal part of
    how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
    Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They
    might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or
    disrupt your visit.
    - Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides.
    These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your
    travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
    - Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But
    they will happen again.
    - The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the
    entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or
    greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this happening in
    the next 50 years (find out more at [af8.org.nz)](https://af8.org.nz/). An earthquake of
    this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.
    **What to do in an earthquake:**
    - DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when
    you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less
    likely you are to be injured.
    - Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers)
    as quickly as possible.
    **Landslides at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - steep mountains around Piopiotahi Milford Sound are prone to rockfall and landslides.
    Earthquakes and severe weather can make the cliffs unstable, sending rock and debris down
    at speed.
    - Smaller rockfalls are common but often go unnoticed, unless you are nearby.
    - Bigger landslides do not happen often. The chance of one occurring during a short visit
    is extremely unlikely. However, they could cause a tsunami in the fiord and do pose a
    risk to life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    - Large earthquakes are the most common trigger of big landslides in Fiordland. A large
    earthquake during your visit is extremely unlikely, especially for a short stay.
    **Be prepared for landslides**
    - Take extra supplies, food, water, first aid, clothes in your vehicle when travelling in
    remote areas, in case you get stuck – The road from Te Anau to Piopiotahi Milford Sound,
    is prone to avalanches, rockfall and landslides. It is monitored 24/7 by the Milford Road
    Alliance. However, if you get stuck, it will take time for help to reach you. Having
    extra supplies in your vehicle will make the wait time more comfortable.
    - If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust clouds, loud rumbling, or
    splashing. Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord
    and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    **Tsunami at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
    - Like all of Aotearoa New Zealand’s coastline, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is at risk of
    tsunami from multiple sources.
    - The most common threat comes from distant earthquakes in the Pacific Ocean. These
    ocean-source tsunamis take hours to reach our shores. Official warnings are issued in
    time for people to move to safety.
    - Less common, but of more concern, is the potential for a large landslide to fall into
    the fiord and trigger a tsunami.
    - Landslide-triggered tsunamis are rare. The chance of one occurring during your visit is
    extremely unlikely. However, they can create large waves and do pose a risk to life at
    Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
    **Be prepared for tsunamis**
    - Triggered by an earthquake – If you feel a LONG (1 minute or more) or STRONG (cannot
    stand up) earthquake, while at Piopiotahi Milford Sound, Get GONE. Move up and away from
    waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    - Triggered by a landslide – If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust
    clouds, loud rumbling, splashing or unusual water behavior, GET GONE. Move up and away
    from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    **Plans and preparedness**
    - Piopiotahi Milford Sound has emergency response plans. These coordinate multiple
    agencies in a State or Emergency. The plans cover earthquakes, tsunami, landslides,
    avalanches, flooding, severe weather and other emergencies.
    - All tourism operators maintain their own emergency procedures. These integrate with the
    wider response in a State of Emergency.
    - If a large landslide triggers a tsunami, there will be no warning. Emergency support
    will take time to arrive. Visitors and workers should be aware of the risk to life and
    prepared to move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as
    possible.
    For more detailed information, please visit [Emergency Management
    Southland](https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or
    [AF8](https://af8.org.nz/).
    For more detailed information, please visit [Emergency Management
    Southland](https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or
    [AF8](https://af8.org.nz/).
