    - Triggered by an earthquake – If you feel a LONG (1 minute or more) or STRONG (cannot
    stand up) earthquake, while at Piopiotahi Milford Sound, Get GONE. Move up and away from
    waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    - Triggered by a landslide – If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust
    clouds, loud rumbling, splashing or unusual water behavior, GET GONE. Move up and away
    from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
    **Plans and preparedness**
    - Piopiotahi Milford Sound has emergency response plans. These coordinate multiple
    agencies in a State or Emergency. The plans cover earthquakes, tsunami, landslides,
    avalanches, flooding, severe weather and other emergencies.
    - All tourism operators maintain their own emergency procedures. These integrate with the
    wider response in a State of Emergency.
    - If a large landslide triggers a tsunami, there will be no warning. Emergency support
    will take time to arrive. Visitors and workers should be aware of the risk to life and
    prepared to move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as
    possible.
    For more detailed information, please visit [Emergency Management
    Southland](https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or
    [AF8](https://af8.org.nz/).

    [disclaimers] *NEW*
        Milford Sound Risk Disclosure: Visitors to Milford Sound should be aware of various
        natural hazards when going to Milford Sound.
        Aotearoa New Zealand: Powerful natural forces have shaped Aotearoa New Zealand over
        millions of years. Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of
        the Pacific Ocean. They have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.
        Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each
        year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage.
        Understanding the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your
        visit.
        Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one
        of the world’s most spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved
        mountains and deep fiord have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions
        of years.
        The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any
        time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes,
        landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
        It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a
        short stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it
        becomes. Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you
        understand the risks, before you go.
        Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small
        earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland. We don’t feel them and they don’t bother
        us. These small movements are a normal part of how the land works and do not pose a
        risk to people.
        Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
        They might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major
        impacts or disrupt your visit.
        Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides.
        These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your
        travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
        Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit.
        But they will happen again.
        The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the
        entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or
        greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this
        happening in the next 50 years (find out more at af8.org.nz) (https://af8.org.nz/).
        An earthquake of this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and
        surrounding area.
        What to do in an earthquake: DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries
        from earthquakes happen when you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the
        ground/floor you are, the less likely you are to be injured.
        Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and
        rivers) as quickly as possible.
        Landslides at Piopiotahi Milford Sound: steep mountains around Piopiotahi Milford
        Sound are prone to rockfall and landslides. Earthquakes and severe weather can make
        the cliffs unstable, sending rock and debris down at speed.
        Smaller rockfalls are common but often go unnoticed, unless you are nearby.
        Bigger landslides do not happen often. The chance of one occurring during a short
        visit is extremely unlikely. However, they could cause a tsunami in the fiord and do
        pose a risk to life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
        Large earthquakes are the most common trigger of big landslides in Fiordland. A large
        earthquake during your visit is extremely unlikely, especially for a short stay.
        Be prepared for landslides: Take extra supplies, food, water, first aid, clothes in
        your vehicle when travelling in remote areas, in case you get stuck – The road from
        Te Anau to Piopiotahi Milford Sound, is prone to avalanches, rockfall and landslides.
        It is monitored 24/7 by the Milford Road Alliance. However, if you get stuck, it will
        take time for help to reach you. Having extra supplies in your vehicle will make the
        wait time more comfortable.
        If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust clouds, loud rumbling, or
        splashing. Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the
        fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
        Tsunami at Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Like all of Aotearoa New Zealand’s coastline,
        Piopiotahi Milford Sound is at risk of tsunami from multiple sources.
        The most common threat comes from distant earthquakes in the Pacific Ocean. These
        ocean-source tsunamis take hours to reach our shores. Official warnings are issued in
        time for people to move to safety.
        Less common, but of more concern, is the potential for a large landslide to fall into
        the fiord and trigger a tsunami.
        Landslide-triggered tsunamis are rare. The chance of one occurring during your visit
        is extremely unlikely. However, they can create large waves and do pose a risk to
        life at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
        Be prepared for tsunamis: Triggered by an earthquake – If you feel a LONG (1 minute
        or more) or STRONG (cannot stand up) earthquake, while at Piopiotahi Milford Sound,
        Get GONE. Move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as
        possible.
        Triggered by a landslide – If you see or hear a landslide entering the water, dust
        clouds, loud rumbling, splashing or unusual water behavior, GET GONE. Move up and
        away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
        Plans and preparedness: Piopiotahi Milford Sound has emergency response plans. These
        coordinate multiple agencies in a State or Emergency. The plans cover earthquakes,
        tsunami, landslides, avalanches, flooding, severe weather and other emergencies.
        All tourism operators maintain their own emergency procedures. These integrate with
        the wider response in a State of Emergency.
        If a large landslide triggers a tsunami, there will be no warning. Emergency support
        will take time to arrive. Visitors and workers should be aware of the risk to life
        and prepared to move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as
        possible.
        For more detailed information, please visit Emergency Management Southland
        (https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or AF8
        (https://af8.org.nz/).

    Cleveland.

    ###AHOY CAPTAIN!
    Thanks for booking in with Adventure sailing, we look forward to getting you out on the
    water for your RST!
    ##Please meet at 9am at Port Geographe Marina, at the Adventure Sailing Office directly
    behind the marina office.
    We are usually finished by 2-3pm.
    (2/21 Spinnaker Blvd, Geographe, 6280, WA)
    ***You will need to find our classroom as per the directions above as google maps will
    just bring you to the marina entrance.***
    In preparation for your upcoming [Recreational Skipper ticket
    course](https://www.transport.wa.gov.au/imarine/recreational-skippers-ticket.asp) you are
    required to obtain some paperwork to meet the Department of Transport requirements.
    ***If you have booked someone else in, please make sure they read this confirmation email
    and the reminder email.***
    ##Please select your appropriate group.
    1. ***Over 18 with drivers licence*** You simply bring your WA drivers licence with you
    on the day of your course.
    2. ***Under 18 with drivers licence or learners permit*** You will need your licence or
    learners permit with this [Parent consent
    form](https://www.transport.wa.gov.au/mediaFiles/marine/MAC_F_ProFormaLetterOfConsent.pdf).
    3. ***Under 18 NO LICENCE or Learners Permit***
    • You need this [Parent consent
    form](https://www.transport.wa.gov.au/mediaFiles/marine/MAC_F_ProFormaLetterOfConsent.pdf).
    • A completed [Eyesight
    test](https://www.transport.wa.gov.au/mediaFiles/marine/MAC_F_RST_Eyesight.pdf) (must be
    done by GP, Optometrist or Registered nurse) Must be done on the attached form. DO NOT DO
    MEDICAL UNLESS YOU HAVE A CONDITION THAT WOULD AFFECT YOUR ABILITY TO DRIVE A BOAT.
    • ID. (The easiest ID is a AUST passport less than 2 years old) If you don’t have a
    passport other methods that are acceptable are listed on page 10 of your attached [RST
    Workbook](https://www.transport.wa.gov.au/mediaFiles/marine/MAC_P_RST_Workbook7.pdf).
    4. ***IT IS A REQUIREMENT THAT YOU WILL COMPLETE THE PRE-COURSE STUDY!***
    Please DO NOT turn up until you have done this!
    This means completing the [ONLINE THEORY TRAINING COURSE, PRACTICAL TRAINING VIDEO &
    QUIZZES](https://seasoaringmarine.com/register/adventure-sailing-rst-online-theory-training-course/?ca=2321f8587da49fc396cab722442812de).
    Please study well. You MUST complete the course above before arriving on the day of your
    course. With the above link to the online course, you will be required to make a login.
    The course will take you 1.5 to 2 hours to complete.
    This is your boating driver’s licence, and you will NOT be awarded this licence if you do
    not pass.
    For reference here is a copy of the [DOT Skippers ticket
    handbook](https://www.transport.wa.gov.au/mediaFiles/marine/MAC_P_RST_Workbook2024.pdf),
    Once you have all your paperwork sorted you are ready to do the course.
    Please use the link provided below to log in, create your own password and to access our
    Online RST Theory Training Course and Practical Assessment Videos. Please check your spam
    or trash folders in case sitting there. This is compulsory viewing before attending your
    RST course.
    We will be monitoring your progress online and if you have not completed all 5 theory
    training modules and clicked on Complete Course after watching the Practical Assessment
    video, you will be unable to attend the course on the booked date. If you do not pass the
    theory test on the allocated day you will need to reschedule another theory assessment,
    on another day, at no extra charge.
    ##PLEASE BRING
    • RELEVENT PAPERWORK & ID
    • HAT (and Sun/wind/rain proof gear depending on weather forecast)
    • WATERBOTTLE & LUNCH
    • SHOES
    You must bring your Driver’s Licence (or Learner’s Permit) with you as we use this to
    satisfy ID and eyesight requirements.
    (If you don't have a drivers licence please bring relevant ID [Proof of ID
    Info](https://www.transport.wa.gov.au/imarine/how-to-get-an-rst.asp)
    ##WE PROVIDE
    • Instructors & Boats
    • Sunscreen
    • Test papers
    • Assessment and Certificates
    • Insurance
    ##Checklist
    • ID (Passport or Drivers licence) [Other ID options listed here]
    (https://www.transport.wa.gov.au/licensing/identity/prove-your-identity/identity-requirements-existing)
    • Eyesight test if required
    • Medical if required (only if you have a medical condition that could affect driving a
    boat)
    • Parent consent (if under 18yo)
    • Have completed the online course and quizzes
    • Hat
    • Water bottle & Lunch
    • Shoes
    ##See you soon for a great day of learning!
    For more info or questions **please do not reply to this email** as we won't see it!
    Send an email to [hello@adventuresailing.com.au] (hello@adventuresailing.com.au) or call
    0428372931
    www.adventuresailing.com.au

    **ARRIVAL**
    • Please arrive at our shop by 9.00am for the tour briefing
    • Please call us if you are running late
    • 466 Macquarie St, South Hobart
    **SHUTTLE TO THE SUMMIT**
    • Departs 9.30am
    **GETTING TO OUR SHOP**
    • Our shop is a 6-minute drive or 25-minute walk from the Hobart city centre.
    **TAXI**
    • Hobart has Uber. A local taxi number is 131008.
    **PARKING**
    • You can usually find free on-street parking on nearby Washington St or Wentworth St.
    **PRE-TOUR DRINK/SNACK**
    • Next door to our shop is Ginger Brown Cafe; great coffee, breakfast, and lunch.
    • On the other side is Macquarie Store, perfect for snacks.
    **WHAT TO WEAR**
    • Check the weather forecast and dress appropriately.
    • Wear comfortable active clothing suitable for riding.
    • The summit can be up to 10°C cooler than sea level.
    • Extra jackets and gloves are available if needed.
    • Bring a lightweight rain jacket if wet weather is possible.
    • Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes.
    • On wet days, consider bringing spare clothes for after the ride.
    **BRING**
    • A lightweight backpack (really useful for carrying any extra gear).
    • Mobile phone
    • Drink & snack (bikes are fitted with a bottle cage)
    • Sunblock, personal medication.
    **SUMMIT CLOSURE**
    If the summit is not accessible due to road closures or poor weather, we will extend the
    ride on the rainforest trail. This trail is much lower on the mountain and is less
    affected by poor weather.
    Please don’t hesitate to contact us if you have any questions.

    ## Thank You for Booking with Canyoning New Zealand!
    We're excited to welcome you on our **Mt Earnslaw Heli Canyoning Adventure** and can't
    wait to share one of New Zealand’s most spectacular wilderness experiences with you.
    ## Before Your Adventure
    ### Meeting Location
    **Queenstown Accommodation Pick Up!**
    Your guides will pick you up from your personal accommodation for 08.15am. We should
    already have your pick up address from your booking form.
    ### What to Bring
    Please bring:
    * Swimwear to wear under your wetsuit
    * A towel for after the adventure
    * A personal water bottle
    * Any personal medications you may require
    For your peace of mind, we recommend leaving unnecessary valuables at home.
    Your dry clothes and personal belongings can be stored in our locked vehicle while you
    are in the canyon. While we have never experienced any security issues, we still
    recommend bringing only what you need for the adventure.
    ### Lunch
    A fresh picnic-style lunch is included and will be provided during the day.
    ### Important Safety Information
    Please take the time to review our risk acknowledgement Information before your
    adventure:
    **[Please Read](https://www.canyoningnewzealand.co.nz/safety/)**
    Please contact us before your tour if you have any injuries, medical conditions, or
    concerns about your suitability for the activity. Please also note that all bookings are
    subject to our 48-hour cancellation policy.
    ### Need Assistance?
    Our friendly reservations team is here to help.
    **Phone:** +64 3 428 0071
    **Open daily:** 8:00am – 8:00pm
    ### Tiaki Promise
    New Zealand is a truly special place, and everyone who lives here or visits has a
    responsibility to help protect it. The Tiaki Promise is a commitment to care for
    Aotearoa, now and for future generations.
    By embracing the Tiaki Promise, you are choosing to act as a guardian — respecting the
    land, protecting the environment, and preserving the natural beauty we are privileged to
    explore.
    **Nau mai, haere mai ki Aotearoa — Welcome to New Zealand!**
    **[Learn more](https://www.tiakinewzealand.com/en_NZ/)**
    ### Help Keep New Zealand Wild
    We're committed to reducing our environmental impact and offsetting our carbon footprint
    by planting native trees throughout the Wakatipu region.
    If you'd like to support this initiative, you can make a voluntary $5 contribution here:
    **[Donate
    Now](https://fareharbor.com/embeds/book/canyoningnewzealand/items/387858/calendar/?flow=489300&full-items=yes)**
    Thank you for choosing Canyoning New Zealand. We look forward to sharing an unforgettable
    day of adventure, wilderness and incredible scenery with you.
    See you soon!
